sentences.zh: 文徵明，長洲人，初名璧，以字行，更字徵仲，別號衡山。

translations.literal: Wen Zhengming was a native of Changzhou. His original name was Bi; he went by his courtesy name, then changed it to Zhengzhong, with the style name Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhengming was from Changzhou. He was originally named Bi, went by his courtesy name, later changed it to Zhengzhong, and took the style name Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 父林，溫州知府。

translations.literal: His father Lin was prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lin served as prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 叔父森，右僉都御史。

translations.literal: His uncle Sen was Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Sen was Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 林卒，吏民醵千金為賻。

translations.literal: When Lin died, officials and commoners pooled a thousand taels of silver as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin died, local officials and people pooled a thousand taels of silver as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 徵明年十六，悉卻之。

translations.literal: Zhengming was sixteen and refused all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengming was sixteen and refused every bit of it.

sentences.zh: 吏民修故卻金亭，以配前守何文淵，而記其事。

translations.literal: The officials and people restored the old Declined-Gold Pavilion to pair with the former prefect He Wenyuan and recorded the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners restored the old Declined-Gold Pavilion to honor the former prefect He Wenyuan alongside Lin and recorded what had happened.

sentences.zh: 徵明幼不慧，稍長，穎異挺發。

translations.literal: Zhengming was dull as a child; when he grew somewhat older, outstanding talent suddenly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhengming was not quick; when he grew older, his talent suddenly blossomed.

sentences.zh: 學文於吳寬，學書於李應禎，學畫於沈周，皆父友也。

translations.literal: He studied literature under Wu Kuan, calligraphy under Li Yingzhen, and painting under Shen Zhou—all were his father's friends.
translations.idiomatic: He studied literature with Wu Kuan, calligraphy with Li Yingzhen, and painting with Shen Zhou, all friends of his father.

sentences.zh: 又與祝允明、唐寅、徐禎卿輩相切劘，名日益著。

translations.literal: He also closely matched wits with Zhu Yunming, Tang Yin, Xu Zhenqing, and their circle, and his fame grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: He also honed himself alongside Zhu Yunming, Tang Yin, Xu Zhenqing, and their circle, and his fame grew by the day.

sentences.zh: 其為人和而介。

translations.literal: In conduct he was gentle yet principled.
translations.idiomatic: In character he was mild yet firm.

sentences.zh: 巡撫俞諫欲遺之金，指所衣藍衫，謂曰：「敝至此邪？

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Yu Jian wished to give him gold and, pointing at the blue robe he wore, said, "So worn as this?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Yu Jian wanted to give him gold. Pointing at the blue robe he wore, he said, "So worn as this?"

sentences.zh: 」徵明佯不喻，曰：「遭雨敝耳。

translations.literal: Zhengming pretended not to understand and said, "It is only worn from the rain."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengming feigned not to understand and said, "It is only worn from the rain."

sentences.zh: 」諫竟不敢言遺金事。

translations.literal: Jian in the end did not dare speak of giving gold.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Jian did not dare mention giving gold.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠慕其名，貽書幣聘之，辭病不赴。

translations.literal: Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao admired his name and sent letters and gifts to engage him; he pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao admired his reputation and sent letters and gifts to engage him; he pleaded illness and would not go.

sentences.zh: 正德末，巡撫李充嗣薦之，會徵明亦以歲貢生詣吏部試，奏授翰林院待詔。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhengde reign, Grand Coordinator Li Chongsi recommended him; at the same time Zhengming also went to the Ministry of Personnel as a tribute student for examination and was appointed Hanlin Academy awaiting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengde reign, Grand Coordinator Li Chongsi recommended him; Zhengming had also gone to the Ministry of Personnel as a tribute student for examination and was appointed Hanlin Academy awaiting edicts.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，預修《武宗實錄》，侍經筵，歲時頒賜，與諸詞臣齒。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded, he took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong, attended the classics lecture, received seasonal gifts, and ranked with the other literary officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, he helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong, attended the classics lecture, received seasonal gifts, and stood among the literary officials.

sentences.zh: 而是時專尚科目，徵明意不自得，連歲乞歸。

translations.literal: But at that time the examination system alone was prized; Zhengming was ill at ease and asked to retire year after year.
translations.idiomatic: But the age prized only the examination track; Zhengming was ill at ease and asked to retire year after year.

sentences.zh: 先是，林知溫州，識張璁諸生中。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lin was prefect of Wenzhou, he had known Zhang Cong among the students.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Lin was prefect of Wenzhou, he had known Zhang Cong among the students.

sentences.zh: 璁既得勢，諷征明附之，辭不就。

translations.literal: When Cong gained power, he hinted that Zhengming should join him; he declined and would not.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cong gained power, he hinted that Zhengming should join him; Zhengming declined.

sentences.zh: 楊一清召入輔政，徵明見獨後。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing was summoned to assist in government; Zhengming alone came to see him last.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing was summoned to assist in government; Zhengming alone came to see him last.

sentences.zh: 一清亟謂曰：「子不知乃翁與我友邪？

translations.literal: Yiqing urgently said to him, "Do you not know that your father and I were friends?"
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing said urgently, "Do you not know your father and I were friends?"

sentences.zh: 」徵明正色曰：「先君棄不肖三十餘年，苟以一字及者，弗敢忘，實不知相公與先君友也。

translations.literal: Zhengming said with a stern face, "My late father left this unworthy son more than thirty years ago. If even one word of his had reached me, I would not dare forget it; I truly did not know that the Grand Secretary and my late father were friends."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengming said sternly, "My late father left this unworthy son more than thirty years ago. If even one word of his had reached me, I would not dare forget it; I truly did not know you and my late father were friends."

sentences.zh: 」一清有慚色，尋與璁謀，欲徙徵明官。

translations.literal: Yiqing looked ashamed; soon he and Cong plotted to transfer Zhengming's post.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing looked ashamed; soon he and Cong plotted to transfer Zhengming's post.

sentences.zh: 徵明乞歸益力，乃獲致仕。

translations.literal: Zhengming pressed his request to retire all the harder and at last obtained leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengming pressed his request to retire all the harder and at last obtained leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 四方乞詩文書畫者，接踵於道，而富貴人不易得片楮，尤不肯與王府及中人，曰：「此法所禁也。

translations.literal: Those from all quarters who begged for his poems, prose, calligraphy, and paintings crowded the road, yet the wealthy and noble could not easily obtain a single sheet; he especially would not give to princely establishments or eunuchs, saying, "The law forbids this."
translations.idiomatic: Those from all quarters who begged for his poems, prose, calligraphy, and paintings crowded the road, yet the wealthy and noble could not easily obtain a single sheet; he especially would not give to princely establishments or eunuchs, saying, "The law forbids this."

sentences.zh: 」周、徽諸王以寶玩為贈，不啟封而還之。

translations.literal: The princes of Zhou and Hui and others sent precious curios as gifts; he returned them unopened.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Zhou and Hui and others sent precious curios as gifts; he returned them unopened.

sentences.zh: 外國使者道吳門，望里肅拜，以不獲見為恨。

translations.literal: Foreign envoys passing through Wu Gate bowed respectfully toward his lane and regretted that they could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys passing through Wu Gate bowed respectfully toward his lane and regretted that they could not see him.

sentences.zh: 文筆遍天下，門下士贗作者頗多，徵明亦不禁。

translations.literal: His writings spread through the realm; many among his followers forged his work, and Zhengming did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: His writings spread through the realm; many among his followers forged his work, and Zhengming did not forbid it.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年卒，年九十矣。

translations.literal: He died in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing, aged ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing, aged ninety.

sentences.zh: 長子彭，字壽承，國子博士。

translations.literal: His eldest son Peng, style name Shoucheng, was a Doctor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Peng, style name Shoucheng, was a Doctor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 次子嘉，字休承，和州學正。

translations.literal: His second son Jia, style name Xiucheng, was Director of Studies in He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jia, style name Xiucheng, was Director of Studies in He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 並能詩，工書畫篆刻，世其家。

translations.literal: Both could write poetry and were skilled in calligraphy, painting, and seal carving, carrying on the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Both could write poetry and were skilled in calligraphy, painting, and seal carving, carrying on the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 彭孫震孟，自有傳。

translations.literal: Peng's grandson Zhenmeng has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Peng's grandson Zhenmeng has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 吳中自吳寬、王鏊以文章領袖館閣，一時名士沈周、祝允明輩與並馳騁，文風極盛。

translations.literal: In Wu, from the time Wu Kuan and Wang Ao led the literary world in the Hanlin, famous men such as Shen Zhou and Zhu Yunming raced alongside them, and literary fashion was at its height.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, from the time Wu Kuan and Wang Ao led the literary world in the Hanlin, famous men such as Shen Zhou and Zhu Yunming raced alongside them, and literary fashion was at its height.

translations.idiomatic: He styled himself the Recluse of Linwu and had two collections, Linwu and Nanguan.

sentences.zh: 自負甚高。

translations.literal: He thought very highly of himself.
translations.idiomatic: He thought very highly of himself.

translations.literal: In prose he took the Qin and Han as his model.
translations.idiomatic: In prose he took the Qin and Han as his model.

sentences.zh: 或謂其詩似李賀，羽曰：「吾詩求出魏、晉上，今乃為李賀邪！

translations.literal: Some said his poetry resembled Li He's; Yu said, "My poetry seeks to rise above Wei and Jin; and now I am Li He!"
translations.idiomatic: Some said his poetry resembled Li He's; Yu said, "My poetry seeks to rise above Wei and Jin; and now I am Li He!"

translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wang Shouren and Zhan Ruoshui and also learned poetry from Li Mengyang.

translations.literal: His writings include the Collected Works of the Mount Wuyue Man.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include the Collected Works of the Mount Wuyue Man.

translations.idiomatic: His son Jishui, style name Chunfu, had a literary reputation and studied calligraphy under Zhu Yunming.

translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Jiajing and was made a Hanlin Bachelor.

translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong disliked him and sent him out as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments; he was promoted in time to Education Intendant of Guangxi.

translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong, style name Lüji, with the style name Yayi.

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Cai Yu and lived at Linwu for three years; afterward he read books at Stone Lake.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Cai Yu and lived at Linwu for three years; afterward he read books at Stone Lake.

translations.literal: As a student he entered the National University by tribute; he died at only forty.
translations.idiomatic: As a student he entered the National University by tribute; he died at only forty.

sentences.zh: 行楷得晉法，書無所不觀。

translations.literal: His regular and running script attained Jin methods; in calligraphy there was nothing he did not study.
translations.idiomatic: His regular and running script attained Jin methods; in calligraphy there was nothing he did not study.

sentences.zh: 陸師道，字子傳。

translations.literal: Lu Shidao, style name Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shidao, style name Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 由進士授工部主事，改禮部，以養母請告歸。

translations.literal: As a jinshi he was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works, transferred to the Ministry of Rites, and asked leave to return home to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: As a jinshi he was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works, transferred to the Ministry of Rites, and asked leave to return home to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 歸而游徵明門，稱弟子。

translations.literal: After returning he studied at Zhengming's gate and called himself his disciple.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he studied at Zhengming's gate and called himself his disciple.

sentences.zh: 家居十四年，乃復起，累官尚寶少卿。

translations.literal: He lived at home fourteen years before taking office again and rose in time to Junior Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home fourteen years before taking office again and rose in time to Junior Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia.

sentences.zh: 善詩文，工小楷古篆繪事。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry and prose and adept at small regular script, ancient seal script, and painting.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in poetry and prose and adept at small regular script, ancient seal script, and painting.

sentences.zh: 人謂徵明四絕，不減趙孟頫，而師道並傳之，其風尚亦略相似。

translations.literal: People said Zhengming's four excellences were not inferior to Zhao Mengfu's, and Shidao transmitted them as well; their fashion was also much the same.
translations.idiomatic: People said Zhengming's four excellences were not inferior to Zhao Mengfu's, and Shidao transmitted them as well; their fashion was also much the same.

sentences.zh: 平居不妄交游，長吏罕識其面。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he did not associate lightly; senior officials rarely knew his face.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary life he did not associate lightly; senior officials rarely knew his face.

translations.idiomatic: His daughter, styled Qingzi, married Zhao Huangguang; husband and wife were both well known in their time.

translations.idiomatic: Chen Daofu, personal name Chun, went by his courtesy name.

translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiong was Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 淳受業徵明，以文行著，善書畫，自號白陽山人。

translations.literal: Chun studied under Zhengming, was noted for literary conduct, was skilled in calligraphy and painting, and styled himself the Recluse of Baiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chun studied under Zhengming, was noted for literary conduct, was skilled in calligraphy and painting, and styled himself the Recluse of Baiyang.

translations.idiomatic: Wang Guxiang, style name Luzhi.

translations.idiomatic: As a jinshi he was made a Hanlin Bachelor and served in turn as an outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 忤尚書汪鋐，左遷真定通判以歸。

translations.literal: He offended Minister Wang Zhen and was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Zhending before returning home.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Minister Wang Zhen and was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Zhending before returning home.

sentences.zh: 與師道俱有清望。

translations.literal: He and Shidao both enjoyed a pure reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shidao both enjoyed a pure reputation.

translations.literal: Qian Gu, style name Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gu, style name Shubao.

sentences.zh: 天球以書，谷以畫，皆繼徵明表表吳中者也。

translations.literal: Tianqiu was famed for calligraphy and Gu for painting; both were eminent successors to Zhengming in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqiu was famed for calligraphy and Gu for painting; both were eminent successors to Zhengming in Wu.

sentences.zh: 其後，華亭何良俊亦以歲貢生入國學。

translations.literal: After them, He Liangjun of Huating also entered the National University as a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: After them, He Liangjun of Huating also entered the National University as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 當路知其名，用蔡羽例，特授南京翰林院孔目。

translations.literal: Those in power knew his name; following Cai Yu's precedent, he was specially appointed Registrar of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power knew his name; following Cai Yu's precedent, he was specially appointed Registrar of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 良俊，字元朗。

translations.literal: Liangjun, style name Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjun, style name Yuanlang.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，二十年不下樓，與弟良傅並負俊才。

translations.literal: From youth he studied devotedly and for twenty years did not come downstairs; he and his younger brother Liangfu both possessed outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied devotedly and for twenty years did not come downstairs; he and his younger brother Liangfu both possessed outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 良傅舉進士，官南京禮部郎中，而良俊猶滯場屋，與上海張之象，同里徐獻忠、董宜陽友善，並有聲。

translations.literal: Liangfu passed the jinshi and served as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, while Liangjun still languished in the examination halls; with Zhang Zhixiang of Shanghai and his fellow townsman Xu Xianzhong and Dong Yiyang he was friendly, and all had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu passed the jinshi and served as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, while Liangjun still languished in the examination halls; with Zhang Zhixiang of Shanghai and his fellow townsman Xu Xianzhong and Dong Yiyang he was friendly, and all had a reputation.

sentences.zh: 及官南京，趙貞吉、王維楨相繼掌院事，與相得甚歡。

translations.literal: When he took office in Nanjing, Zhao Zhenji and Wang Weizhen in succession headed the academy, and they got on very well together.
translations.idiomatic: When he took office in Nanjing, Zhao Zhenji and Wang Weizhen in succession headed the academy, and they got on very well together.

sentences.zh: 良俊居久之，慨然嘆曰：「吾有清森閣在海上，藏書四萬卷，名畫百簽，古法帖彝鼎數十種，棄此不居，而僕僕牛馬走乎！

translations.literal: After Liangjun had been there a long time, he sighed and said, "I have the Clear-Forest Pavilion on the sea with forty thousand volumes, a hundred famous paintings, and dozens of ancient model calligraphies, bronzes, and tripods—yet I abandon this and run about like a drudge!"
translations.idiomatic: After Liangjun had been there a long time, he sighed and said, "I have the Clear-Forest Pavilion on the sea with forty thousand volumes, a hundred famous paintings, and dozens of ancient model calligraphies, bronzes, and tripods—yet I abandon this and run about like a drudge!"

sentences.zh: 」遂移疾歸。

translations.literal: He then resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He then resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 海上中倭，復居金陵者數年，更買宅居吳閶。

translations.literal: When pirates struck on the coast he lived in Jinling again for several years, then bought a house and dwelt in Wu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates struck on the coast he lived in Jinling again for several years, then bought a house and dwelt in Wu Gate.

sentences.zh: 年七十始返故里。

translations.literal: Only at seventy did he return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Only at seventy did he return to his native place.

sentences.zh: 徐獻忠，字伯臣。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhong, style name Bochen.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhong, style name Bochen.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，舉於鄉，官奉化知縣。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Fenghua.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing reign he passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 著書數百卷。

translations.literal: He wrote several hundred juan of books.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote several hundred juan of books.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十七，王世貞私諡曰貞憲。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-seven; Wang Shizhen privately gave him the posthumous title Zhenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-seven; Wang Shizhen privately gave him the posthumous title Zhenxian.

sentences.zh: 董宜陽，字子元。

translations.literal: Dong Yiyang, style name Ziyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yiyang, style name Ziyuan.

sentences.zh: 張之象，字月鹿。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhixiang, style name Yuelu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhixiang, whose style name was Yuelu,

sentences.zh: 祖萱，湖廣參議。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan was a participant in administration in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan had served as a participant in administration in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 父鳴謙，順天通判。

translations.literal: His father Mingqian was assistant prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mingqian was assistant prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 之象由諸生入國學，授浙江按察司知事，以吏隱自命。

translations.literal: Zhixiang entered the National University as a student and was appointed an official in the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission, styling himself a recluse among clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang entered the National University as a student and was appointed an official in the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission, taking himself for a recluse among clerks.

sentences.zh: 歸益務撰著。

translations.literal: After returning home he devoted himself all the more to writing.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he devoted himself all the more to writing.

sentences.zh: 晚居秀林山，罕入城市。

translations.literal: In his later years he lived on Mount Xiulin and rarely entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he lived on Mount Xiulin and rarely went into town.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十一。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 黄佐附 歐大任 黎民表

translations.literal: Huang Zuo, appendix: Ou Daren, Li Minbiao
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zuo, with appendixes: Ou Daren and Li Minbiao

sentences.zh: 黃佐，字才伯，香山人。

translations.literal: Huang Zuo, style name Caibo, was a native of Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zuo, style name Caibo, was from Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 祖瑜，長樂知縣，以學行聞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was magistrate of Changle and was known for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had been magistrate of Changle and was known for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 正德中，佐舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign he took first place in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde reign he took first place in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，始成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor succeeded, he at last became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, he at last became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，授編修，陳初政要務，又請修舉新政，疏皆留中。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing he was appointed Compiler, set forth essentials of the new reign's policies, and also asked to restore and promote the new policies; his memorials were all kept within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing he was appointed Compiler, set forth essentials of the new reign's policies, and also asked to restore and promote the new policies; his memorials were all kept within the palace.

sentences.zh: 尋省親歸，便道謁王守仁，與論知行合一之旨，數相辨難，守仁亦稱其直諒。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home to visit his parents and, by the way, called on Wang Shouren; they discussed the doctrine of the unity of knowledge and action and repeatedly argued back and forth; Shouren also praised his straightforwardness and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went home to visit his parents and, taking a detour, called on Wang Shouren; they discussed the unity of knowledge and action and argued back and forth repeatedly; Shouren also praised his frank sincerity.

sentences.zh: 還朝，會出諸翰林為外僚，除江西僉事。

translations.literal: When he returned to court, it happened that Hanlin scholars were sent out as outer officials; he was appointed Jiangxi Surveillance Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court, Hanlin scholars were being sent out as outer officials; he was appointed Jiangxi Surveillance Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旋改督廣西學校，聞母病，引疾乞休，不俟報竟去，下巡撫林富逮問。

translations.literal: He was soon changed to supervise schools in Guangxi; hearing his mother was ill, he pleaded illness and asked to retire, left without awaiting reply, and Grand Coordinator Lin Fu had him seized and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned to supervise schools in Guangxi; when he heard his mother was ill, he pleaded illness and asked to retire, left without awaiting a reply, and Grand Coordinator Lin Fu had him seized and questioned.

sentences.zh: 富言佐誠有罪，第為親受過，於情可原，乃令致仕。

translations.literal: Fu said Zuo was indeed guilty, but that he had erred for his parent's sake and could be excused on human grounds; he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said Zuo was indeed guilty, but that he had erred for his parent's sake and could be excused on human grounds; he was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 家居九年，簡宮僚，命以編修兼司諫，尋進侍讀，掌南京翰林院。

translations.literal: After nine years at home, palace attendants were selected; he was ordered to serve as Compiler and concurrently Remonstrating Official, soon promoted to Reader-in-Waiting, and directed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years at home, palace attendants were selected; he was ordered to serve as Compiler and concurrently Remonstrating Official, soon promoted to Reader-in-Waiting, and directed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 召為右諭德，擢南京國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Instructor of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Chancellor of the Nanjing National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Right Instructor of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Chancellor of the Nanjing National University.

sentences.zh: 母憂除服，起少詹事。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended, he was raised to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for his mother ended, he was raised to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 謁大學士夏言，與論河套事不合。

translations.literal: He called on Grand Secretary Xia Yan and disagreed with him over the Ordos affair.
translations.idiomatic: He called on Grand Secretary Xia Yan and disagreed with him over the Ordos affair.

sentences.zh: 會吏部缺左侍郎，所司推禮部右侍郎崔桐及佐。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ministry of Personnel lacked a Left Vice Minister; the responsible office recommended Right Vice Minister of Rites Cui Tong and Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Ministry of Personnel lacked a Left Vice Minister; the responsible office recommended Right Vice Minister of Rites Cui Tong and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 給事中徐霈、御史艾樸言：「桐與左侍郎許成名競進，至相詬詈；

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Xu Pei and the censor Ai Pu said: "Tong and Left Vice Minister Xu Chengming competed for advancement, even reviling each other;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xu Pei and Censor Ai Pu said, "Tong and Left Vice Minister Xu Chengming competed for advancement, even reviling each other;

sentences.zh: 而佐及同官王用賓亦爭覬望，惟恐或先之，宜皆止勿用。

translations.literal: while Zuo and his colleague Wang Yongbin also strove for preferment, each fearing the other might get ahead; all should be stopped and not employed."
translations.idiomatic: while Zuo and his colleague Wang Yongbin also strove for preferment, each fearing the other might get ahead; all should be stopped and not employed."

sentences.zh: 」言從中主之，遂皆賜罷。

translations.literal: Yan followed the court's ruling; all were dismissed by imperial gift.
translations.idiomatic: Yan followed the court's ruling; all were dismissed by imperial gift.

sentences.zh: 佐學以程、硃為宗，惟理氣之說，獨持一論。

translations.literal: Zuo's learning took Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi as its core; on the doctrine of principle and material force alone he held a single view.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's learning took Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi as its core; on the doctrine of principle and material force alone he held a single view.

sentences.zh: 平生譔述至二百六十余卷。

translations.literal: In his lifetime his writings reached more than two hundred and sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Over his lifetime his writings reached more than two hundred and sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 所著《樂典》，自謂泄造化之秘。

translations.literal: In his work Music Canon he claimed to disclose the secret of creation's transformations.
translations.idiomatic: In his Music Canon he claimed to disclose the secret of creation's transformations.

sentences.zh: 年七十七卒。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 穆宗詔贈禮部右侍郎，諡文裕。

translations.literal: The Muzong Emperor ordered him posthumously made Right Vice Minister of Rites with the posthumous title Wenyü.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong ordered him posthumously made Right Vice Minister of Rites with the posthumous title Wenyü.

sentences.zh: 佐弟子多以行業自飭，而梁有譽、歐大任、黎民表詩名最著雲。

translations.literal: Many of Zuo's disciples disciplined themselves in conduct, while Liang Youyu, Ou Daren, and Li Minbiao were most famed in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Zuo's disciples disciplined themselves in conduct, while Liang Youyu, Ou Daren, and Li Minbiao were most famed in poetry.

sentences.zh: 歐大任，字楨伯，順德人。

translations.literal: Ou Daren, style name Zhenbo, was a native of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Ou Daren, style name Zhenbo, was from Shunde.

sentences.zh: 由歲貢生歷官南京工部郎中，年八十而終。

translations.literal: From tribute student he served in turn as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and died at eighty.
translations.idiomatic: From tribute student he served in turn as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 黎民表，字惟敬，從化人，御史貫子也。

translations.literal: Li Minbiao, style name Weijing, was a native of Conghua and son of the censor Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Minbiao, style name Weijing, was from Conghua and son of the censor Guan.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試，久不第，授翰林孔目，遷吏部司務。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination but long failed the metropolitan; he was appointed Hanlin Registrar and transferred to a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination but long failed the metropolitan; he was appointed Hanlin Registrar and transferred to a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 執政知其能文，用為制敕房中書，供事內閣，加官至參議。

translations.literal: Those in power knew he could write and used him as a drafter in the Edict Drafting Office, serving in the Grand Secretariat; he rose in rank to Participant.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power knew he could write and used him as a drafter in the Edict Drafting Office, serving in the Grand Secretariat; he rose in rank to Participant.

sentences.zh: 柯維騏

translations.literal: Ke Weiji
translations.idiomatic: Ke Weiji

sentences.zh: 柯維騏，字奇純，莆田人。

translations.literal: Ke Weiji, style name Qichun, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Weiji, style name Qichun, was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 高祖潛，翰林學士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qian was a Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qian was a Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 父英，徽州知府。

translations.literal: His father Ying was prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying was prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 維騏舉嘉靖二年進士，授南京戶部主事，未赴，輒引疾歸。

translations.literal: Weiji passed the jinshi in the second year of Jiajing and was appointed a principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; before taking up the post he at once pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Weiji passed the jinshi in the second year of Jiajing and was appointed a principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; before taking up the post he at once pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 張孚敬用事，創新制，京朝官病滿三年者，概罷免，維騏亦在罷中。

translations.literal: When Zhang Fuling was in power he created a new rule: capital officials who had been ill three full years were all dismissed, and Weiji was among those dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fuling was in power he created a new rule: capital officials who had been ill three full years were all dismissed, and Weiji was among those dismissed.

sentences.zh: 自是謝賓客，專心讀書。

translations.literal: From then on he declined guests and devoted himself to reading.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he declined guests and devoted himself to reading.

sentences.zh: 久之，門人日進，先後四百餘人，維騏引掖靡倦。

translations.literal: After a long time his disciples increased daily; more than four hundred came in succession, and Weiji guided and supported them without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time his disciples increased daily; more than four hundred came in succession, and Weiji guided and supported them without weariness.

sentences.zh: 慨近世學者樂徑易而憚積累，竊二氏之說以文其固陋也，作左右二銘，訓學者務實。

translations.literal: Lamenting that scholars of recent times delighted in shortcuts and feared accumulated effort, borrowing the teachings of the two heterodox schools to adorn their obstinate ignorance, he wrote two inscriptions, left and right, instructing students to seek what is solid.
translations.idiomatic: Lamenting that scholars of recent times delighted in shortcuts and feared accumulated effort, borrowing the teachings of the two heterodox schools to adorn their obstinate ignorance, he wrote two inscriptions, left and right, instructing students to seek what is solid.

sentences.zh: 以辨心術、端趨向為實志，以存敬畏、密操履為實功，而其極則以宰理人物、成能天地為實用，作講義二卷。

translations.literal: He took discerning the mind's methods and rectifying one's orientation as solid purpose, preserving reverence and tightening conduct as solid effort, and at the utmost taking ordering human affairs and fulfilling heaven and earth's capacity as solid application, and wrote two juan of lecture notes.
translations.idiomatic: He took discerning the mind's methods and rectifying one's orientation as solid purpose, preserving reverence and tightening conduct as solid effort, and at the utmost taking ordering human affairs and fulfilling heaven and earth's capacity as solid application, and wrote two juan of lecture notes.

sentences.zh: 《宋史》與《遼》、《金》二《史》，舊分三書，維騏乃合之為一，以遼、金附之，而列二王於本紀。

translations.literal: The History of Song and the two histories of Liao and Jin had formerly been divided into three books; Weiji combined them into one, attached Liao and Jin to it, and placed the two [Southern Song] emperors in the basic annals.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Song and the two histories of Liao and Jin had formerly been divided into three books; Weiji combined them into one, attached Liao and Jin to it, and placed the two [Southern Song] emperors in the basic annals.

sentences.zh: 褒貶去取，義例嚴整，閱二十年而始成，名之曰《宋史新編》。

translations.literal: In praise and blame, inclusion and exclusion, the principles and categories were strict and orderly; after twenty years it was completed and named New Compilation of the History of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In praise and blame, inclusion and exclusion, the principles and categories were strict and orderly; after twenty years it was completed and named New Compilation of the History of Song.

sentences.zh: 又著《史記考要》、《續莆陽文獻志》，及所作詩文集並行於世。

translations.literal: He also wrote Investigations into the Records of the Grand Historian and Continued Gazetteer of Putian Literature, and his collected poetry and prose circulated together in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Investigations into the Records of the Grand Historian and Continued Gazetteer of Putian Literature, and his collected poetry and prose circulated together in the world.

sentences.zh: 維騏登第五十載，未嘗一日服官。

translations.literal: Weiji passed the jinshi in the fiftieth year and never served in office a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Weiji passed the jinshi in the fiftieth year and never served in office a single day.

sentences.zh: 中更倭亂，故廬焚燬，家困甚，終不妄取。

translations.literal: In the midst of this came the pirate turmoil; his old house was burned and his family was very poor, yet in the end he took nothing he ought not.
translations.idiomatic: In the midst of this came the pirate turmoil; his old house was burned and his family was very poor, yet in the end he took nothing he ought not.

sentences.zh: 世味無所嗜，惟嗜讀書。

translations.literal: He cared for nothing in worldly taste and cared only for books.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for nothing in worldly taste and cared only for books.

sentences.zh: 撫按監司時有論薦，不復起。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and the like sometimes recommended him, but he did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and the like sometimes recommended him, but he did not take office again.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，廷臣復薦。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing the court officials again recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing the court officials again recommended him.

sentences.zh: 所司以維騏年高，但授承德郎致仕。

translations.literal: The responsible office, because Weiji was advanced in years, only granted him Gentleman for Promoting Virtue and retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office, because Weiji was advanced in years, only granted him Gentleman for Promoting Virtue and retirement.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十有八。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 孫茂竹，海陽知縣。

translations.literal: His grandson Maozhu was magistrate of Haiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Maozhu was magistrate of Haiyang.

sentences.zh: 茂竹子昶，副都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: Maozhu's son Chang was Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhu's son Chang was Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 王慎中附 屠應埈 等

translations.literal: Wang Shenzhong, appendix: Tu Yingjun and others
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenzhong, with appendix: Tu Yingjun and others

sentences.zh: 王慎中，字道思，晉江人。

translations.literal: Wang Shenzhong, style name Daosi, was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenzhong, style name Daosi, was from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 四歲能誦詩，十八舉嘉靖五年進士，授戶部主事，尋改禮部祠祭司。

translations.literal: At four he could recite poetry; at eighteen he passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing and was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, soon transferred to the Sacrificial Rites Bureau of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At four he could recite poetry; at eighteen he passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing and was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, soon transferred to the Sacrificial Rites Bureau of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時四方名士唐順之、陳束、李開先、趙時春、任瀚、熊過、屠應埈、華察、陸銓、江以達、曾忭輩，咸在部曹。

translations.literal: At that time famous men from all quarters—Tang Shunzhi, Chen Shu, Li Kaixian, Zhao Shichun, Ren Han, Xiong Guo, Tu Yingjun, Hua Cha, Lu Quan, Jiang Yida, Zeng Ning, and their circle—were all in the ministry bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: At that time famous men from all quarters—Tang Shunzhi, Chen Shu, Li Kaixian, Zhao Shichun, Ren Han, Xiong Guo, Tu Yingjun, Hua Cha, Lu Quan, Jiang Yida, Zeng Ning, and their circle—were all in the ministry bureaus.

sentences.zh: 慎中與之講習，學大進。

translations.literal: Shenzhong studied with them and his learning advanced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhong studied with them and his learning advanced greatly.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔簡部郎為翰林，眾首擬慎中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year an edict selected ministry directors for the Hanlin; the multitude first proposed Shenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year an edict selected ministry directors for the Hanlin; the multitude first proposed Shenzhong.

sentences.zh: 大學士張孚敬欲一見，辭不赴，乃稍移吏部，為考功員外郎，進驗封郎中。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Fuling wished to see him once; he declined and did not go, and was then slightly transferred to the Ministry of Personnel as an outer-section secretary in the Bureau of Evaluations, advancing to director in the Bureau of Honors and Seals.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Fuling wished to see him once; he declined and did not go, and was then slightly transferred to the Ministry of Personnel as an outer-section secretary in the Bureau of Evaluations, advancing to director in the Bureau of Honors and Seals.

sentences.zh: 忌者讒之孚敬，因覆議真人張衍慶請封疏，謫常州通判。

translations.literal: Envious men slandered him to Fuling; because of a renewed discussion of the True Man Zhang Yanqing's request for enfeoffment memorial, he was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Envious men slandered him to Fuling; because of a renewed discussion of the True Man Zhang Yanqing's request for enfeoffment memorial, he was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷戶部主事、禮部員外郎，並在南京。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Rites, both in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Rites, both in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢山東提學僉事，改江西參議，進河南參政。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted Education Intendant of Shandong, changed to Jiangxi Administrative Commissioner, and advanced to Administrative Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was promoted Education Intendant of Shandong, changed to Jiangxi Administrative Commissioner, and advanced to Administrative Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 侍郎王杲奉命振荒，以其事委慎中，還朝，薦慎中可重用。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Gao was ordered to relieve famine and entrusted the matter to Shenzhong; on returning to court he recommended Shenzhong as fit for heavy use.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Gao was ordered to relieve famine and entrusted the matter to Shenzhong; on returning to court he recommended Shenzhong as fit for heavy use.

sentences.zh: 會二十年大計，吏部注慎中不及。

translations.literal: It happened to be the great evaluation of the twentieth year; the Ministry of Personnel did not list Shenzhong among those promoted.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be the great evaluation of the twentieth year; the Ministry of Personnel did not list Shenzhong among those promoted.

sentences.zh: 而大學士夏言先嘗為禮部尚書，慎中其屬吏也，與相忤，遂內批不謹，落其職。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xia Yan had formerly been Minister of Rites; Shenzhong had been his subordinate and clashed with him, so an inner court note called him uncareful and he lost his post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xia Yan had formerly been Minister of Rites; Shenzhong had been his subordinate and clashed with him, so an inner court note called him uncareful and he lost his post.

sentences.zh: 慎中為文，初主秦、漢，謂東京下無可取。

translations.literal: In writing, Shenzhong at first upheld Qin and Han and said nothing after the Eastern Han was worth taking.
translations.idiomatic: In writing, Shenzhong at first upheld Qin and Han and said nothing after the Eastern Han was worth taking.

sentences.zh: 已悟歐、曾作文之法，乃盡焚舊作，一意師仿，尤得力於曾鞏。

translations.literal: When he understood the methods of Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong in composition, he burned all his old work and devoted himself to imitation, gaining special strength from Zeng Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When he understood the methods of Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong in composition, he burned all his old work and devoted himself to imitation, gaining special strength from Zeng Gong.

sentences.zh: 順之初不服，久亦變而從之。

translations.literal: Shunzhi at first did not approve; after a long time he too changed and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi at first did not approve; after a long time he too changed and followed.

sentences.zh: 壯年廢棄，益肆力古文，演迤詳贍，卓然成家，與順之齊名，天下稱之曰王、唐，又曰晉江、毘陵。

translations.literal: Cast aside in his prime, he all the more threw himself into ancient-style prose, expansive, detailed, and ample, and established a school of his own; he was famed alongside Shunzhi, and the realm called them Wang and Tang, also Jinjiang and Biling.
translations.idiomatic: Cast aside in his prime, he all the more threw himself into ancient-style prose, expansive, detailed, and ample, and established a school of his own; he was famed alongside Shunzhi, and the realm called them Wang and Tang, also Jinjiang and Biling.

sentences.zh: 家居，問業者踵至。

translations.literal: Living at home, those who came to ask instruction crowded in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Living at home, those who came to ask instruction crowded in succession.

sentences.zh: 年五十一而終。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 李攀龍、王世貞後起，力排之，卒不能掩。

translations.literal: Li Panlong and Wang Shizhen rose later and strove to exclude him, but in the end could not obscure him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Panlong and Wang Shizhen rose later and strove to exclude him, but in the end could not obscure him.

sentences.zh: 攀龍，慎中提學山東時所賞拔者也。

translations.literal: Panlong was one Shenzhong had favored and promoted when he was Education Intendant of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong was one Shenzhong had favored and promoted when he was Education Intendant of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 慎中初號遵岩居士，後號南江。

translations.literal: Shenzhong's first style was Recluse of Zunyan; his later style was Nanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhong's first style was Recluse of Zunyan; his later style was Nanjiang.

sentences.zh: 屠應埈，字文升，平湖人，刑部尚書勛子也。

translations.literal: Tu Yingjun, style name Wensheng, was a native of Pinghu and son of the Minister of Punishments Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Yingjun, style name Wensheng, was from Pinghu and son of the Minister of Punishments Xun.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 由郎中改翰林，官至右諭德。

translations.literal: From director he was changed to the Hanlin and rose to Right Instructor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: From director he was changed to the Hanlin and rose to Right Instructor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 華察，字子潛，無錫人。

translations.literal: Hua Cha, style name Ziqian, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Cha, style name Ziqian, was from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 應埈同年進士。

translations.literal: Yingjun's fellow graduate in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow jinshi of the same year as Yingjun.

sentences.zh: 累官侍講學士，掌南京翰林院。

translations.literal: He rose in time to Erudite Lecturer and directed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in time to Erudite Lecturer and directed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 陸銓，字選之，鄞人。

translations.literal: Lu Quan, style name Xuanzhi, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Quan, style name Xuanzhi, was from Yin.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 與弟編修釴爭大禮，並系詔獄，被杖，後官廣西布政使。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother, Compiler Yi, disputed the Great Rites; both were imprisoned by imperial order and beaten; he later served as Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother, Compiler Yi, disputed the Great Rites; both were imprisoned by imperial order and beaten; he later served as Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 釴終山東提學副使，兄弟皆能文。

translations.literal: Yi ended as Vice Education Intendant of Shandong; both brothers could write.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ended as Vice Education Intendant of Shandong; both brothers could write.

sentences.zh: 江以達，字子順，貴溪人。

translations.literal: Jiang Yida, style name Zishun, was a native of Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yida, style name Zishun, was from Guixi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 累官福建提學僉事。

translations.literal: He rose in time to Education Intendant of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in time to Education Intendant of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 高叔嗣附 蔡汝楠

translations.literal: Gao Shusi, appendix: Cai Runan
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shusi, with appendix: Cai Runan

sentences.zh: 高叔嗣，字子業，祥符人。

translations.literal: Gao Shusi, style name Ziye, was a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shusi, style name Ziye, was from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 年十六，作《申情賦》幾萬言，見者驚異。

translations.literal: At sixteen he wrote the Rhapsody on Declared Feeling of nearly ten thousand words; those who saw it were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he wrote the Rhapsody on Declared Feeling of nearly ten thousand words; those who saw it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 十八舉於鄉，第嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: At eighteen he passed the provincial examination and ranked as jinshi in the second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the provincial examination and ranked as jinshi in the second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授工部主事，改吏部。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 歷稽勛郎中。

translations.literal: He served in turn as director in the Bureau of Honors and Seals.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as director in the Bureau of Honors and Seals.

sentences.zh: 出為山西左參政，斷疑獄十二事，人稱為神。

translations.literal: Sent out as Left Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi, he decided twelve doubtful legal cases; people called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as Left Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi, he decided twelve doubtful legal cases; people called him divine.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣按察使，卒官，年三十有七。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang and died in office at the age of thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Huguang Surveillance Commissioner, he died in that post at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 叔嗣少受知邑人李夢陽，及官吏部，與三原馬理、武城王道同署，以文藝相磨切。

translations.literal: Shusi from youth received recognition from fellow townsman Li Mengyang; when he reached office in the Ministry of Personnel, he was in the same bureau as Ma Li of Sanyuan and Wang Daotong of Wucheng, and they sharpened one another through letters and the arts.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gao Shusi won the patronage of his townsman Li Mengyang; once he served in the Ministry of Personnel, he shared a desk with Ma Li of Sanyuan and Wang Daotong of Wucheng and they honed one another in literature.

sentences.zh: 其為詩，清新婉約，雖為夢陽所知，不宗其說。

translations.literal: In his composing of poetry, it was fresh, clear, and graceful; though known to Mengyang, he did not take his school as master.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was fresh and graceful; though Mengyang knew him, he did not follow the Former Seven Masters.

sentences.zh: 陳束序其《蘇門集》，謂有應物之沖澹，兼曲江之沈雄，體王、孟之清適，具高、岑之悲壯。

translations.literal: Chen Shu preface to his "Sumen Collection" said it had Yingwu's serene simplicity, together with Qujiang's profound grandeur, embodied Wang and Meng's clarity and ease, and possessed Gao and Cen's tragic heroism.
translations.idiomatic: In his preface to the "Sumen Collection," Chen Shu wrote that the work had Wei Yingwu's serene simplicity and Zhang Ji's solemn power, the clarity of Wang Wei and Meng Haoran, and the tragic grandeur of Gao Shi and Cen Shen.

sentences.zh: 王世貞則曰：「子業詩，如高山鼓琴，沈思忽往，木葉盡脫，石氣自青；

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen then said: "Ziye's poetry is like drumming the zither on a high mountain—deep thought suddenly departs; tree leaves all fall away, and stone breath turns green of itself;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen remarked, "Ziye's verse is like playing the zither on a lofty peak—thought sinks deep and then soars; the leaves fall bare, and the very stone seems to breathe green;

sentences.zh: 又如衛洗馬言愁，憔瘁婉篤，令人心折。

translations.literal: again like the Commandant of Wei speaking of sorrow—haggard, graceful, and sincere, making people's hearts break.
translations.idiomatic: and again like Wei Jie speaking of grief—wan, tender, and piercing, until the heart cannot bear it;

sentences.zh: 」而蔡汝楠至推為本朝第一雲。

translations.literal: " and Cai Runan even ranked him first in the dynasty, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: " Cai Runan went so far as to call him the finest poet of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 兄仲嗣，官知府，亦有才名。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhongsi served as prefect and also had a name for talent.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhongsi, who became a prefect, was likewise famed for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 汝楠，字子木。

translations.literal: Runan, style name Zimu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Runan, courtesy name Zimu.

sentences.zh: 兒時隨父南京，聽祭酒湛若水講學，輒有解悟。

translations.literal: In childhood he followed his father to Nanjing; hearing Rector Zhan Ruoshui lecture, he immediately had understanding.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he accompanied his father to Nanjing; listening to Rector Zhan Ruoshui lecture, he grasped the teaching at once.

sentences.zh: 年十八，成嘉靖十一年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he completed the jinshi degree in the eleventh year of Jiajing and was appointed a Court Gentleman for Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination in 1532 and was appointed a courier in the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 從王慎中、唐順之及叔嗣輩學為詩。

translations.literal: He followed Wang Shenzhong, Tang Shunzhi, and Shusi's circle in learning to compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He studied poetry with Wang Shenzhong, Tang Shunzhi, and Gao Shusi and his peers.

sentences.zh: 尋進刑部員外郎，徙南京刑部。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and then transferred to its Nanjing branch.

sentences.zh: 善皇甫涍兄弟，尚書顧璘引為忘年友。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with the Huangfu Qin brothers; Minister Gu Lin introduced him as a friend despite the gap in years.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to the Huangfu Qin brothers, and Minister Gu Lin took him as a friend despite their difference in age.

sentences.zh: 廷議改歸德州為府，擢汝楠知其府事。

translations.literal: At court it was debated to change Guidezhou into a prefecture; Runan was promoted to administer that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated elevating Guidezhou to a prefecture, Runan was appointed to govern it.

sentences.zh: 以母憂歸，聚諸生石鼓書院，與說經。

translations.literal: Returning on mourning for his mother, he gathered students at Shigu Academy and expounded the classics to them.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he withdrew home, gathered students at Shigu Academy, and lectured on the classics.

sentences.zh: 治民有惠政，既去，士民祠祀之。

translations.literal: In governing the people he had benevolent policies; after he departed, scholars and commoners enshrined and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule brought real benefit to the people, and after he left office scholars and townsfolk set up a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 歷官江西左、右布政使，擢右副都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In successive offices he was Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, then promoted Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right administration commissioner of Jiangxi, then was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 召為兵部右侍郎，從諸大僚祝釐西宮，世宗望見其貌寢，改南京工部右侍郎，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Summoned as Right Vice Minister of War, he followed the great ministers in blessing rites at the Western Palace; Shizong saw his appearance was poor and changed him to Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Vice Minister of War, he joined the senior ministers in blessing rites at the Western Palace; the emperor, struck by his sickly looks, reassigned him to Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing, where he soon died.

sentences.zh: 汝楠始好為詩，有重名。

translations.literal: Runan at first loved composing poetry and had a weighty name.
translations.idiomatic: Runan began as a poet of considerable renown.

sentences.zh: 中年好經學，及官江西，與鄒守一、羅洪先游，學益進，然詩由此不工去。

translations.literal: In middle age he loved classical learning; when he held office in Jiangxi, he associated with Zou Shouyi and Luo Hongxian, and his learning daily advanced—yet his poetry thereby became less skilled and fell away.
translations.idiomatic: In midlife he turned to classical learning; in Jiangxi he studied with Zou Shouyi and Luo Hongxian and made great progress, but his poetry suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 陳束附 任瀚 熊過 李開先

translations.literal: Chen Shu, appendix: Ren Han, Xiong Guo, Li Kaixian
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shu, with appendixes on Ren Han, Xiong Guo, and Li Kaixian

sentences.zh: 陳束，字約之，鄞人。

translations.literal: Chen Shu, style name Yuezhi, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shu, courtesy name Yuezhi, was from Yin in Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 生而聰慧絕倫，好讀古書。

translations.literal: From birth he was exceptionally intelligent; he loved reading ancient books.
translations.idiomatic: He was prodigiously clever from childhood and devoted himself to ancient texts.

sentences.zh: 會稽侍郎董官翰林時，聞束才，召視之。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister Dong Zhi of Kuaiji was in the Hanlin Academy, hearing of Chen's talent, he summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: While Dong Zhi of Kuaiji was serving in the Hanlin Academy as a vice minister, he heard of Chen's gifts and called the boy in to meet him.

sentences.zh: 東垂髫而前，試詞賦立就，遂字以女，攜至京，文譽益起。

translations.literal: Chen came forward while his hair still hung down; tested in rhyme-prose he completed it on the spot; [Dong] gave him a courtesy name with his daughter and brought him to the capital, and his literary reputation rose still higher.
translations.idiomatic: The boy came forward with his hair still in childhood locks, wrote a fu on command at once, and Dong betrothed his daughter to him and took him to the capital, where Chen's literary fame soared.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年廷對，世宗親擢羅洪先、程文德、楊名為一甲，而置唐順之及束、任瀚於二甲，皆手批其卷。

translations.literal: In the palace examination of the eighth year of Jiajing, Shizong personally placed Luo Hongxian, Cheng Wende, and Yang Ming in the top grade, while setting Tang Shunzhi together with Chen and Ren Han in the second grade—all with handwritten comments on their papers.
translations.idiomatic: At the 1529 palace examination the Jiajing Emperor personally ranked Luo Hongxian, Cheng Wende, and Yang Ming first class, placing Tang Shunzhi, Chen Shu, and Ren Han in the second class, each paper bearing the emperor's own marginal comments.

sentences.zh: 無何，考庶吉士，得胡經等二十人，以束及順之、瀚曾奉御批，列經等首。

translations.literal: Before long, in the examination for Hanlin academicians, Hu Jing and twenty others were obtained; because Chen together with Tang and Ren had once received imperial marginal comments, they were listed at the head of Hu Jing and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, in the Hanlin examination, Hu Jing and twenty others passed; because Chen, Tang, and Ren had received the emperor's marginal notes, they were placed ahead of the rest.

sentences.zh: 座主張璁、霍韜以前此館選悉改他曹，引嫌，亦議改，乃寢前令，束授禮部主事。

translations.literal: Chief examiners Zhang Cong and Huo Tao, because on the previous occasion Hanlin selections had all been changed to other offices, cited bias and also debated a change; the earlier order was then suspended, and Chen was appointed a Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The chief examiners Zhang Cong and Huo Tao, citing the precedent that prior Hanlin picks had been reassigned to other agencies, debated overturning the list; the earlier ranking was set aside, and Chen was made a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時有「嘉靖八才子」之稱，謂束及王慎中、唐順之、趙時春、熊過、任瀚、李開先、呂高也。

translations.literal: At the time there was the title "Eight Talents of Jiajing," meaning Chen together with Wang Shenzhong, Tang Shunzhi, Zhao Shichun, Xiong Guo, Ren Han, Li Kaixian, and Lü Gao.
translations.idiomatic: They were known as the "Eight Talents of the Jiajing reign": Chen Shu, Wang Shenzhong, Tang Shunzhi, Zhao Shichun, Xiong Guo, Ren Han, Li Kaixian, and Lü Gao.

sentences.zh: 四郊改建，都御史汪鋐請徙近郊居民墳墓，束疏諫，不報。

translations.literal: When the four suburban altars were rebuilt, Grand Coordinator Wang Zhen requested relocating the graves of residents near the suburbs; Chen memorialized in remonstrance, but there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebuilding of the suburban altars, Grand Coordinator Wang Zhen proposed moving nearby graves; Chen submitted a memorial in protest, but it went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 遷員外郎，改編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director and then changed to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director and later made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 束出璁、韜門，不肯親附。

translations.literal: Chen came from Zhang and Huo's school but was unwilling to attach himself closely.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chen had studied under Zhang Cong and Huo Tao, he refused to court them.

sentences.zh: 歲時上壽，望門投刺，輒馳馬過之。

translations.literal: At the seasonal birthday congratulations, he would look toward their gates and cast visiting cards, then gallop past.
translations.idiomatic: On their birthdays he would ride up, toss in a calling card, and gallop away without stopping.

sentences.zh: 為所惡，出為湖廣僉事。

translations.literal: Hated by them, he was sent out as Vice Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: They turned on him, and he was posted out as a vice commissioner in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 分巡辰、沅，治有聲。

translations.literal: Inspecting Chen and Yuan, his governance had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector of Chen and Yuan prefectures, he earned a strong reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 稍遷福建參議，改河南提學副使。

translations.literal: He was somewhat promoted to Administration Commissioner of Fujian and then changed to Education Vice Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administration commissioner of Fujian and was later transferred to education vice commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 束故有嘔血疾，會科試期近，試八郡之士，三月而畢，疾增劇，竟不起，年才三十有三。

translations.literal: Chen had long suffered an illness of vomiting blood; when the provincial examination period drew near, he tested scholars of the eight prefectures and finished in three months; his illness grew severe and he finally could not rise—his years were only thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had long suffered hemoptysis; as the provincial exams approached he examined candidates from eight prefectures in three exhausting months, his illness worsened, and he died at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 妻董，亦能詩，束卒未幾亦卒，束竟無後。

translations.literal: His wife Dong could also compose poetry; not long after Chen died she too died, and Chen in the end had no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Dong, was also a poet; she died soon after he did, and Chen left no heirs.

sentences.zh: 當嘉靖初，稱詩者多宗何、李，束與順之輩厭而矯之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, those who spoke of poetry mostly took He and Li as masters; Chen and Tang's circle were weary of this and reacted against it.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jiajing period most poets followed the He-Li school; Chen Shu and Tang Shunzhi's circle rebelled against that fashion.

sentences.zh: 束早世，且藁多散逸，今所傳《後岡集》，僅十之一二雲。

translations.literal: Chen died young, and most of his drafts were scattered and lost; what is transmitted today as the "Hougang Collection" is only one or two tenths, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Chen died young and most of his manuscripts were lost; the "Hougang Collection" that survives represents perhaps a tenth of his work.

sentences.zh: 任瀚，字少海，南充人。

translations.literal: Ren Han, style name Shaohai, was a native of Nanchong.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Han, courtesy name Shaohai, was from Nanchong in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1529.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，未上，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hanlin Academician but, before taking up the post, was appointed a Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for the Hanlin Academy but, before entering, was appointed a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 屢遷考功郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Bureau of Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as director in the Bureau of Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 十八年，簡宮僚，改左春坊左司直兼翰林院檢討。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was selected for palace tutors and was changed to Left Subeditor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1539 he was chosen as a palace tutor and made left subeditor of the heir apparent's left secretariat, with a concurrent post as Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜疏引疾，出郭戒行，疏再上，不報，復自引還。

translations.literal: The next year he submitted a memorial citing illness, went outside the city to bid farewell to his journey, submitted the memorial again, received no reply, and returned on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized illness, went beyond the city walls to take leave of his departure, submitted again without reply, and came back on his own.

sentences.zh: 給事中周來劾瀚舉動任情，蔑視官守。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhou Lai impeached Han, saying his conduct was willful and he despised the duties of office.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Zhou Lai accused Han of acting on whim and scorning his official obligations.

sentences.zh: 帝令自陳，瀚語侵掌詹事霍韜。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him to state his case in his own words; Han's language trespassed against Chief Guardian of the Heir Apparent Huo Tao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a written defense; Han's reply insulted Huo Tao, chief tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，勒為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and stripped him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之，遇赦，復官致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he met an amnesty, was restored to office, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Years later an amnesty restored his rank and he retired.

sentences.zh: 終世宗朝，中外屢薦，不復用。

translations.literal: Throughout the Jiajing reign, inside and outside the court he was repeatedly recommended, but he was never again employed.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Jiajing reign he was recommended repeatedly from within and outside the government, but was never reappointed.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，四川巡撫劉思潔、曾省吾先後疏薦，優旨報聞而已。

translations.literal: When Shenzong succeeded to the throne, Sichuan Grand Coordinators Liu Sijie and Zeng Shengwu in succession memorialized recommending him; only a favorable rescript acknowledging receipt was returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenzong took the throne, the Sichuan grand coordinators Liu Sijie and Zeng Shengwu recommended him in turn, but the court merely acknowledged the memorials without acting.

sentences.zh: 瀚少懷用世志，百家二氏之書，罔不搜討。

translations.literal: Han from youth harbored the ambition to serve the age; books of the hundred schools and the two teachings—none were not searched and investigated.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Han aspired to serve his times and read widely across the hundred schools and the teachings of Buddhism and Daoism.

sentences.zh: 被廢，益反求《六經》，闡明聖學。

translations.literal: After his dismissal he turned all the more to seeking within the Six Classics and elucidated sage learning.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of office, he turned inward to the Six Classics and expounded the teachings of the sages.

sentences.zh: 晚又潛心於《易》，深有所得。

translations.literal: In his later years he again devoted himself quietly to the Changes and gained a deep understanding.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he studied the Book of Changes and arrived at profound insight.

sentences.zh: 文亦高簡。

translations.literal: His writing, too, was lofty and concise.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was likewise elevated and spare.

sentences.zh: 卒年九十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 熊過，字叔仁，富順人。

translations.literal: Xiong Guo, style name Shuren, was a native of Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Guo, courtesy name Shuren, was from Fushun.

sentences.zh: 瀚同年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the same year as Han.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the same year as Ren Han.

sentences.zh: 累官祠祭郎中，坐事貶秩，復除名為民。

translations.literal: He rose in successive offices to Director of Sacrifices; because of an offense his rank was reduced, and he was again stripped of name and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of sacrifices, was demoted for an offense, and was finally dismissed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 李開先，字伯華，章丘人。

translations.literal: Li Kaixian, style name Bohua, was a native of Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kaixian, courtesy name Bohua, was from Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 束同年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the same year as Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Chen Shu.

sentences.zh: 官至太常少卿。

translations.literal: In office he rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 性好蓄書，李氏藏書之名聞天下。

translations.literal: By nature he loved collecting books; the Li family's book collection was famed under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books passionately, and the Li family library was renowned throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 呂高，字山甫，丹徒人。

translations.literal: Lü Gao, style name Shanfu, was a native of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gao, courtesy name Shanfu, was from Dantu.

sentences.zh: 亦束同年進士。

translations.literal: He, too, was a jinshi in the same year as Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He too graduated as a jinshi alongside Chen Shu.

sentences.zh: 歷官山東提學副使。

translations.literal: In successive offices he was Education Vice Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as education vice commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 鄉試錄文，舊多出學使者手，巡按御史葉經乞順之文。

translations.literal: The examination record essays for the provincial test had long mostly come from the education intendant's own hand; Touring Censor Ye Jing requested Tang Shunzhi's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial examination essays were traditionally drafted by the education intendant; the touring censor Ye Jing asked Tang Shunzhi to write the report instead.

sentences.zh: 高心憾，寓書京師友人言經紕繆。

translations.literal: Gao resented this and sent a letter to a friend in the capital saying Jing was in error.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gao took offense and wrote to a friend in the capital accusing Ye Jing of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩惡經，遂置之死。

translations.literal: Yan Song hated Jing and thus had him put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song, who hated Ye Jing, had him executed.

sentences.zh: 及後大計，諸御史謂經禍由高，乃斥歸，於八子中，名最下。

translations.literal: At the later grand assessment the various censorial officials said Jing's calamity arose from Gao, and he was dismissed and sent home; among the eight, his name stood lowest.
translations.idiomatic: At the next grand evaluation the censors blamed Ye Jing's death on Lü Gao, who was dismissed; of the Eight Talents his reputation sank lowest.

sentences.zh: 田汝成子 藝蘅

translations.literal: Tian Rucheng, son: Yiheng
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rucheng, with his son Yiheng

sentences.zh: 田汝成，字叔禾，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Tian Rucheng, style name Shuhe, was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rucheng, courtesy name Shuhe, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1526.

sentences.zh: 授南京刑部主事，尋召改禮部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Principal Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and soon summoned to be transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and was soon transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月上言：「陛下以青宮久虛，祈天建醮，復普放生之仁，凡羈蹄釒殺羽禁在上林者，咸獲縱釋。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year he memorialized upward, saying: "Your Majesty, because the Eastern Palace has long stood vacant, prayed to Heaven and established fasting altars, and again extended the universal benevolence of releasing life—all hobbled hooves, birds and beasts with feathers confined in Shanglin Park have alike obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of 1531 he submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty, because the heir apparent's quarters have long stood empty, has prayed to Heaven and held ritual fasts, and again shown mercy by releasing living creatures—every hobbled beast and every bird and beast penned in Shanglin has been set free.

sentences.zh: 顧使囹圄之徒久纏徽纆，衣冠之侶流竄窮荒，父子長離，魂魄永喪，此獨非陛下之赤子乎！

translations.literal: Yet you allow those long entangled in the cangue within prisons, and gentry companions exiled to remote wastes—father and son long separated, souls forever lost: are these alone not Your Majesty's children!
translations.idiomatic: Yet prisoners remain shackled for years, and officials in exile wander the wilderness, fathers and sons torn apart and souls lost forever—are they not also Your Majesty's children?

sentences.zh: 望大廣皇仁，悉加寬宥。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will greatly broaden imperial benevolence and extend leniency to all alike.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to extend this mercy and grant a broad amnesty.

sentences.zh: 」忤旨，切責，停俸二月。

translations.literal: " It offended the imperial intent; he was severely reprimanded and his salary was suspended for two months.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial angered the emperor, who rebuked him sharply and suspended his salary for two months.

sentences.zh: 屢遷祠祭郎中，廣東僉事，謫知滁州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of Sacrifices, Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, and demoted to magistrate of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of sacrifices and Guangdong vice commissioner, then was demoted to magistrate of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 復擢貴州僉事，改廣西右參議，分守右江。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Commissioner of Guizhou, changed to Right Administration Commissioner of Guangxi, and assigned to guard the Right River.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Guizhou vice commissioner, then made right administration commissioner of Guangxi with charge of the Right River circuit.

sentences.zh: 龍州土酋趙楷、憑祥州土酋李寰皆弒主自立，與副使翁萬達密討誅之。

translations.literal: The tribal chieftain Zhao Kai of Longzhou and the tribal chieftain Li Huan of Pingxiang both murdered their lords and seized power for themselves; together with Vice Commissioner Weng Wanda they secretly planned their execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kai of Longzhou and Li Huan of Pingxiang both murdered their chiefs and seized power; Rucheng and Vice Commissioner Weng Wanda secretly plotted to kill them.

sentences.zh: 努灘賊侯公丁為亂，斷藤峽群賊與相應。

translations.literal: The bandit Hou Gongding of Nutan made rebellion, and the bandits of the Broken Vine Gorge group responded in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Gongding of Nutan rebelled, and the bandits of Broken Vine Gorge rose with him.

sentences.zh: 汝成復偕萬達設策誘擒公丁，而進兵討峽賊，大破之，又與萬達建善後七事，一方遂靖，有銀幣之賜。

translations.literal: Rucheng again joined Weng Wanda in setting a stratagem to lure and capture Gongding, then advanced troops to punish the gorge bandits and inflicted a great defeat; together with Wanda he also established seven follow-up measures for pacification, and the region was then settled, for which he received a gift of silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Rucheng and Weng Wanda lured Hou Gongding into capture, then marched against the gorge rebels and routed them; their seven-point pacification plan quieted the region, and the court rewarded them with silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 遷福建提學副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Education Vice Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to education vice commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 歲當大比，預定諸生甲乙。

translations.literal: In the year of the great examination he predetermined the students' order of rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial examinations came, he ranked the candidates in advance.

sentences.zh: 比榜發，一如所定。

translations.literal: When the list was published, it was exactly as he had predetermined.
translations.idiomatic: When the results were posted, the list matched his predictions exactly.

sentences.zh: 汝成博學工古文，尤善敘述。

translations.literal: Rucheng was erudite and skilled in ancient-style prose, especially good at narration.
translations.idiomatic: Rucheng was learned and a master of ancient prose, especially narrative writing.

sentences.zh: 歷官西南，諳曉先朝遺事，撰《炎徼紀聞》。

translations.literal: Holding office in the southwest, he was well versed in relic affairs of the former dynasty and compiled "Records of the Southern March."
translations.idiomatic: Serving in the southwest, he mastered Ming frontier history and wrote the "Records of the Southern March."

sentences.zh: 歸田後，般桓湖山，窮浙西諸名勝，撰《西湖遊覽志》，並見稱於時。

translations.literal: After returning to his fields he roamed the lakes and mountains, exhausted the famous sites of western Zhejiang, and compiled the "Gazetteer of West Lake Sightseeing"—both were acclaimed in the time.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he wandered the lakes and hills of western Zhejiang and wrote the "Gazetteer of West Lake Sightseeing"; both works won contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 他所論著甚多，時推其博洽。

translations.literal: His other writings and discussions were very numerous; contemporaries praised his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote prolifically on many subjects, and his contemporaries admired his erudition.

sentences.zh: 子藝蘅，字子。

translations.literal: His son Yiheng, style name Ziqian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tian Yiheng, courtesy name Ziqian.

sentences.zh: 十歲從父過採石，賦詩有警句。

translations.literal: At age ten he followed his father in passing Ma'anshan and composed poetry with striking lines.
