translations.idiomatic: At ten he traveled with his father past Ma'anshan and wrote a poem with memorable lines.

sentences.zh: 性放誕不羈，嗜酒任俠。

translations.literal: By nature he was unrestrained and unbound, fond of wine and given to chivalric conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was wild and unconventional, devoted to wine and the ways of the knight-errant.

sentences.zh: 以歲貢生為徽州訓導，罷歸。

translations.literal: As a tribute student he became Director of Studies at Huizhou and, dismissed, returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Qualified by tribute student status, he became director of studies at Huizhou, was dismissed, and went home.

sentences.zh: 作詩有才調，為人所稱。

translations.literal: In composing poetry he had literary talent and tone and was praised by people.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry showed real talent and was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 皇甫涍弟 沖 汸 濂

translations.literal: Huangfu Qin, brothers: Chong, Fang, Lian
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Qin, with his brothers Chong, Fang, and Lian

sentences.zh: 皇甫涍，字子安，長洲人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Qin, style name Zi'an, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Qin, courtesy name Zian, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 父錄，弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: His father Lu was a jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huangfu Lu graduated as a jinshi in 1496.

sentences.zh: 任重慶知府。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 生四子，沖、涍、汸、濂。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Chong, Xiao, Fang, and Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons were born to him—Chong, Xiao, Fang, and Lian.

sentences.zh: 沖、汸同登嘉靖七年鄉薦，明年，汸第進士。

translations.literal: Chong and Fang both passed the provincial examination in the seventh year of Jiajing; the next year Fang placed as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Fang both won provincial honors in 1528; the following year Fang passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 又三年，涍第進士。

translations.literal: Three years later Xiao also placed as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on, Xiao too became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 又十三年，濂亦第進士。

translations.literal: Thirteen years after that Lian also placed as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Another thirteen years passed before Lian likewise took his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 而沖尚為舉子。

translations.literal: Yet Chong remained only a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Chong alone never rose beyond the provincial degree.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並好學工詩，稱「皇甫四傑」。

translations.literal: The brothers all loved learning and excelled at poetry, and were called the "Four Champions of the Huangfu."
translations.idiomatic: All four brothers were devoted scholars and poets, famed as the "Four Huangfu Champions."

sentences.zh: 沖，字子浚，善騎射，好談兵。

translations.literal: Chong, style name Zijun, was skilled at horsemanship and archery and loved to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, courtesy name Zijun, rode and shot well and delighted in talk of war.

sentences.zh: 遇南北內訌，譔《幾策》、《兵統》、《枕戈雜言》三書，凡數十萬言。

translations.literal: When civil strife broke out between north and south, he compiled three works—"Several Stratagems," "Military System," and "Pillow-Spear Miscellany"—totaling several hundred thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the north–south turmoil he wrote three books—"Several Stratagems," "Military System," and "Pillow-Spear Miscellany"—running to hundreds of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 涍，初授工部主事，改禮部。

translations.literal: Xiao was first appointed a director in the Ministry of Works, then transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao began as a director in the Ministry of Works and was later moved to Rites.

sentences.zh: 歷儀制員外郎，主客郎中。

translations.literal: He served as an outside director in the Ceremonies Bureau and as a director in the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Ceremonies Bureau to head the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 在儀制時，夏言為尚書，連疏請建儲，皆涍起草，故言深知涍才。

translations.literal: While in Ceremonies, Xia Yan was minister; he repeatedly memorialized to establish an heir, and Xiao drafted every memorial, so Yan came to know his talent well.
translations.idiomatic: During his Ceremonies posting, Minister Xia Yan kept submitting memorials on the succession; Xiao drafted them all, and Yan learned to value his ability.

sentences.zh: 比簡宮僚，遂用為春坊司直兼翰林檢討。

translations.literal: When palace tutors were being selected, he was therefore made a director in the Eastern Palace and concurrently a Hanlin reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen for the palace staff, he was appointed Eastern Palace director and Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 言者論涍改官有私，謫廣平通判，量移南京刑部主事，進員外郎，遷浙江僉事。

translations.literal: Critics charged that Xiao's transfer had been improper; he was demoted to assistant prefect of Guangping, then gradually moved to a director's post in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, promoted to outside director, and transferred to an assistant surveillance commissioner in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of favoritism in his promotion, he was sent down to Guangping as assistant prefect, later served in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, became an outside director, and was posted to Zhejiang as an assistant surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大計京官，以南曹事論罷，邑邑發病卒。

translations.literal: At the grand evaluation of capital officials he was dismissed on a charge related to the southern ministry; dejected, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: When capital officials were reviewed he was removed over a southern ministry matter; heartsick, he took ill and died.

sentences.zh: 涍沈靜寡與，自負高俊，稍不當意，終日相對無一言。

translations.literal: Xiao was reserved and kept few companions; proud of his lofty talent, if anything displeased him he could sit face to face all day without a word.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was quiet and aloof, sure of his own brilliance; the slightest offense could leave him speechless before a guest for an entire day.

sentences.zh: 居官砥廉隅，然頗操切，多忤物，故數被讒謗雲。

translations.literal: In office he polished his integrity, yet he was rather severe and often gave offense, so he was repeatedly slandered, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with scrupulous honesty but was harsh and often crossed others, and so drew repeated calumny.

sentences.zh: 汸，字子循，七歲能詩。

translations.literal: Fang, style name Zixun, could compose poetry at age seven.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, courtesy name Zixun, was writing verse at seven.

sentences.zh: 官工部主事，名動公卿，沾沾自喜，用是貶秩為黃州推官。

translations.literal: As a director in the Ministry of Works his name stirred the great officials; pleased with himself, he was for that reason reduced in rank to magistrate of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in Works, he became the talk of the court; his self-satisfaction cost him a demotion to magistrate of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京稽勛郎中，再貶開州同知，量移處州府同知。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Nanjing Merit Office, demoted again to assistant prefect of Kaizhou, and transferred to assistant prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in Nanjing's Merit Office, was demoted once more to assistant prefect of Kaizhou, and was then moved to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢雲南僉事，以計典論黜。

translations.literal: He was elevated to assistant surveillance commissioner in Yunnan and dismissed at the grand evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Yunnan as an assistant surveillance commissioner, he was removed at the triennial review.

sentences.zh: 汸和易，近聲色，好狎游。

translations.literal: Fang was easygoing, fond of music and women, and given to convivial roaming.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was genial, loved pleasure and company, and wandered freely.

sentences.zh: 於兄弟中最老壽，年八十乃卒。

translations.literal: Among the brothers he lived longest, dying at eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Of the four brothers he lived longest, reaching eighty.

sentences.zh: 濂，字子約，初授工部主事，母喪除，起故官，典惜薪廠。

translations.literal: Lian, style name Ziyue, was first appointed a director in the Ministry of Works; after mourning for his mother he returned to his former post and managed the fuel-wood depot.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, courtesy name Ziyue, began in the Ministry of Works; when his mourning ended he resumed office and oversaw the fuel-wood depot.

sentences.zh: 賈人偽增數罔利，濂按其罪。

translations.literal: A merchant falsely inflated the accounts for profit; Lian prosecuted him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When a merchant padded the books for illicit gain, Lian pressed the case against him.

sentences.zh: 賈人女為尚書文明妾，明召濂切責之。

translations.literal: The merchant's daughter was a concubine of Minister Wang Wenming, who summoned Lian and sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant's daughter had become a concubine of Minister Wang Wenming, who called Lian in and scolded him harshly.

sentences.zh: 濂抗言曰：「公掌邦政，縱奸人干紀，又欲奪郎官法守邪？

translations.literal: Lian answered defiantly, "You hold the nation's government—will you let villains break the law and then seize an officer's duty to uphold it?"
translations.idiomatic: Lian stood his ground: "You govern the realm—will you shelter a lawbreaker and rob an officer of his charge to enforce the law?"

sentences.zh: 」明為斂容謝。

translations.literal: Wenming checked his manner and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Wenming collected himself and apologized.

sentences.zh: 大計，謫河南布政司理問，終興化同知。

translations.literal: At the grand evaluation he was demoted to registrar of the Henan provincial administration commission and ended as assistant prefect of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewed and demoted to registrar in Henan, he finished his career as assistant prefect of Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 濂兄弟與黃魯曾、省曾為中表兄弟，文藻亦相似。

translations.literal: The Lian brothers and Huang Lueng and Shengeng were cousins by marriage, and their literary ornament was much alike.
translations.idiomatic: The Lians were cousins and literary kin to Huang Lueng and Huang Shengeng, and their style was much the same.

sentences.zh: 其後，裡人張鳳翼、燕翼、獻翼並負才名。

translations.literal: Later their townsman Zhang Fengyi, Zhang Yanyi, and Zhang Xianyi all bore reputations for talent.
translations.idiomatic: Later three Zhangs of the same hamlet—Fengyi, Yanyi, and Xianyi—won names for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 吳人語曰：「前有四皇，後有三張。

translations.literal: A Wu saying ran: "Before, four Huangfus; after, three Zhangs."
translations.idiomatic: People in Wu said: "First the four Huangfus, then the three Zhangs."

sentences.zh: 」鳳翼、燕翼終舉人。

translations.literal: Fengyi and Yanyi ended as provincial graduates only.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyi and Yanyi never rose above the provincial degree.

sentences.zh: 而獻翼為太學生，名日益高，年老矣，狂甚，為讎家所殺。

translations.literal: Xianyi was a National University student whose fame grew daily; in old age he grew wildly arrogant and was killed by an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyi studied at the National University and grew ever more celebrated; in his last years his madness provoked a foe who murdered him.

sentences.zh: 茅坤子 維

translations.literal: Mao Kun's son Wei
translations.idiomatic: Mao Kun; his son Wei

sentences.zh: 茅坤，字順甫，歸安人。

translations.literal: Mao Kun, style name Shunfu, was a native of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Kun, courtesy name Shunfu, came from Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1538.

sentences.zh: 歷知青陽、丹徒二縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Qingyang and Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Qingyang and Dantu in turn.

sentences.zh: 母憂，服闋，遷禮部主事，移吏部稽勛司，坐累，謫廣平通判。

translations.literal: After mourning for his mother, when the mourning period ended he was promoted to a director in the Ministry of Rites, moved to the Merit Office in the Ministry of Personnel, and through implicated guilt was demoted to assistant prefect of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he returned as a Rites director, shifted to Personnel's Merit Office, and was demoted to Guangping for guilt by association.

sentences.zh: 屢遷廣西兵備僉事，轄府江道。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to assistant surveillance commissioner for military affairs in Guangxi, with jurisdiction over the Fujiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Guangxi assistant surveillance commissioner for military affairs, overseeing the Fujiang route.

sentences.zh: 坤雅好談兵。

translations.literal: Kun by nature loved to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kun delighted in military talk.

sentences.zh: 瑤賊據鬼子諸砦，殺陽朔令。

translations.literal: Yao bandits held the Guizi stockades and killed the magistrate of Yangshuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yao rebels seized the Guizi forts and slew the magistrate of Yangshuo.

sentences.zh: 朝議大征，總督應檟以問坤。

translations.literal: The court debated a major campaign; Grand Coordinator Ying Song asked Kun's view.
translations.idiomatic: The court planned a great expedition; Grand Coordinator Ying Song sought Kun's counsel.

sentences.zh: 坤曰：「大征非兵十萬不可，餉稱之，今猝不能集，而賊已據險為備。

translations.literal: Kun said, "A major campaign cannot succeed without a hundred thousand troops and commensurate supplies; we cannot gather them at once, while the bandits already hold the passes and stand ready.
translations.idiomatic: Kun replied, "A full campaign needs a hundred thousand men and matching provisions—we cannot muster them overnight, and the rebels already hold the heights.

sentences.zh: 計莫若雕剿。

translations.literal: The best plan is piecemeal extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Better to pick them off one by one.

sentences.zh: 條入殲其魁，他部必襲，謀自全，此便計也。

translations.literal: Execute the chiefs one by one; the other groups will strike on their own to save themselves—this is the expedient plan.
translations.idiomatic: Cut down the leaders in turn; the rest will turn on one another to survive—that is the shrewd course.

sentences.zh: 」檟善之，悉以兵事委坤。

translations.literal: Song approved and entrusted all military affairs to Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Song agreed and gave him full command.

sentences.zh: 連破十七砦，晉秩二等。

translations.literal: He broke seventeen stockades in succession and was promoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen forts fell in succession, and he was raised two grades in rank.

sentences.zh: 民立祠祀之。

translations.literal: The people erected a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 遷大名兵備副使，總督楊博嘆為奇才，特薦於朝。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner for military affairs at Daming; Grand Coordinator Yang Bo sighed that he was a rare talent and specially recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice commissioner at Daming, Yang Bo called him a wonder and sent a special recommendation to court.

sentences.zh: 為忌者所中，追論其先任貪污狀，落職歸。

translations.literal: He was struck by a jealous enemy, who pursued charges of corruption from his earlier post, and he left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A rival brought him down with retroactive charges of graft in his former post, and he retired home.

sentences.zh: 時倭事方急，胡宗憲延之幕中，與籌兵事，奏請為福建副使。

translations.literal: When the pirate crisis was acute, Hu Zongxian kept him in his staff to plan military affairs and memorialized to appoint him vice commissioner in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: As the coastal raids intensified, Hu Zongxian took him onto his staff for military planning and recommended him for Fujian vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 吏部持之，乃已。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel held up the appointment, and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel blocked the appointment, and nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 家人橫於里，為巡按龐尚鵬所劾，遂褫冠帶。

translations.literal: His household servants bullied the neighborhood; Surveillance Commissioner Pang Shangpeng impeached him, and he was stripped of cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: His servants tyrannized the countryside; Pang Shangpeng impeached him, and he lost his rank and insignia.

sentences.zh: 坤既廢，用心計治生，家大起。

translations.literal: Once dismissed, Kun turned to business schemes to make a living, and his household rose greatly in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Out of office, Kun threw himself into trade and speculation until his family grew very rich.

sentences.zh: 年九十，卒於萬曆二十九年。

translations.literal: At ninety he died in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety in 1601.

sentences.zh: 坤善古文，最心折唐順之。

translations.literal: Kun excelled at ancient-style prose and admired Tang Shunzhi above all.
translations.idiomatic: Kun wrote classical prose in the ancient manner and revered Tang Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 順之喜唐、宋諸大家文，所著文編，唐、宋人自韓、柳、歐、三蘇、曾、王八家外，無所取，故坤選《八大家文鈔》。

translations.literal: Shunzhi delighted in the great writers of Tang and Song; in his literary anthology he took no one outside the Tang and Song masters Han Yu, Liu Zongyuan, Ouyang Xiu, the three Sus, Zeng Gong, and Wang Anshi—the Eight Great Masters—so Kun compiled the "Anthology of the Eight Great Masters."
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi favored Tang and Song masters; his own anthology admitted only Han, Liu, Ouyang, the three Sus, Zeng, and Wang—the Eight Great Masters—so Kun edited the "Anthology of the Eight Great Masters."

sentences.zh: 其書盛行海內，鄉里小生無不知茅鹿門者。

translations.literal: The book spread throughout the empire; village lads all knew the name Deer Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The work swept the realm; even village boys knew Deer Gate.

sentences.zh: 鹿門，坤別號也。

translations.literal: Deer Gate was Kun's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Deer Gate was Kun's style name.

sentences.zh: 少子維，字孝若，能詩，與同郡臧懋循、吳稼竳、吳夢陽，並稱四子。

translations.literal: His younger son Wei, style name Xiaoru, could write poetry; with his fellow townsman Zang Maoxun, Wu Jiaqiao, and Wu Mengyang he was called one of the Four Masters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei, courtesy name Xiaoru, was a poet; with Zang Maoxun, Wu Jiaqiao, and Wu Mengyang of the same district he formed the Four Masters.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣闕上書，希得召見，陳當世大事，不報。

translations.literal: He once went to the capital to submit a memorial, hoping to be summoned and to set forth great affairs of the age; he received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He once petitioned at court, hoping for an audience to speak on the great issues of the day, but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 謝榛附 盧柟

translations.literal: Xie Zhen appended: Lu Kan
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhen; appended: Lu Kan

sentences.zh: 謝榛，字茂秦，臨清人。

translations.literal: Xie Zhen, style name Maoqin, was a native of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhen, courtesy name Maoqin, came from Linqing.

sentences.zh: 眇一目。

translations.literal: He was blind in one eye.
translations.idiomatic: One eye was sightless.

sentences.zh: 年十六，作樂府商調，少年爭歌之。

translations.literal: At sixteen he composed yuefu in the shang mode, and young men vied to sing them.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he wrote shang-mode ballads that youths raced to sing.

sentences.zh: 已，折節讀書，刻意為歌詩。

translations.literal: Later he restrained himself to study and labored to write songs and poems.
translations.idiomatic: Later he disciplined himself in books and strove at poetry and song.

sentences.zh: 西游彰德，為趙康王所賓禮。

translations.literal: Traveling west to Zhangde, he was honored as a guest by Prince Kang of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Going west to Zhangde, he became a honored guest of Prince Kang of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 入京師，脫盧柟於獄。

translations.literal: Entering the capital, he secured Lu Kan's release from prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he won Lu Kan's freedom from jail.

sentences.zh: 當七子結社之始，尚論有唐諸家，各有所重。

translations.literal: At the founding of the Seven Masters' society they still debated the Tang masters, each favoring his own.
translations.idiomatic: When the Seven Masters first formed their league, they still disputed which Tang poets to esteem.

sentences.zh: 榛曰：「取李、杜十四家最勝者，熟讀之以會神氣，歌詠之以求聲調，玩味之以裒精華。

translations.literal: Zhen said, "Take the finest of the fourteen Li and Du lines, read them thoroughly to absorb their spirit, sing them to seek their tone, and savor them to gather their essence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "Choose the best of Li Bai's and Du Fu's fourteen modes, read until their spirit enters you, chant until you catch their music, taste until you distill their marrow.

sentences.zh: 得經三要，則浩乎渾淪，不必塑謫仙而畫少陵也。

translations.literal: Grasp the three essentials of the classics and you will be vast and whole—there is no need to mold a statue of the Banished Immortal or paint a portrait of Young Du."
translations.idiomatic: Master the three essentials of the canon and your work will roll like the flood—there is no need to carve Li Bai or paint Du Fu."

sentences.zh: 」諸人心師其言，厥後雖合力擯榛，其稱詩指要，實自榛發也。

translations.literal: The others took his words as their guide; though later they united to ostracize Zhen, the essentials of their poetics in fact began with him.
translations.idiomatic: All took him as teacher; though they later drove him out together, their poetic creed truly began with Zhen.

sentences.zh: 盧柟，字少楩，浚縣人。

translations.literal: Lu Kan, style name Shaoqian, was a native of Jun County.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kan, courtesy name Shaoqian, came from Jun County.

sentences.zh: 家素封，輸貲為國學生。

translations.literal: His family had long been wealthy; he paid fees to enter the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a rich house, he bought his way into the National University.

sentences.zh: 博聞強記，落筆數千言。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with a powerful memory, he could set down several thousand words at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was wide and his memory keen; thousands of words flowed from his brush at once.

sentences.zh: 為人跅馳，好使酒罵座。

translations.literal: By nature he was unrestrained, fond of wine, and given to reviling guests at table.
translations.idiomatic: He was wild, loved wine, and often abused his dinner guests.

sentences.zh: 常為具召邑令，日晏不至，柟大怒，徹席滅炬而臥。

translations.literal: He once prepared a feast and summoned the county magistrate; when evening came and the magistrate had not arrived, Kan flew into a rage, cleared the table, and extinguished the lamps to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: He once set a banquet for the county magistrate; when dusk passed with no guest, Kan raged, swept away the dishes, put out the lights, and lay down.

sentences.zh: 令至，柟已大醉，不具賓主禮。

translations.literal: When the magistrate arrived, Kan was already very drunk and did not observe the rites between host and guest.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate came at last to find Kan drunk past courtesy.

sentences.zh: 會柟役夫被榜，他日牆壓死，令即捕柟，論死，系獄，破其家。

translations.literal: Soon a laborer of Kan's was flogged; another day a wall collapsed and killed him; the magistrate at once arrested Kan, sentenced him to death, imprisoned him, and ruined his family.
translations.idiomatic: When a servant of Kan's was beaten and later crushed by a falling wall, the magistrate seized Kan, condemned him to death, threw him in prison, and beggared his house.

sentences.zh: 里中兒為獄卒，恨柟，笞之數百，謀以土囊壓殺之，為他卒救解。

translations.literal: A village youth serving as a jailer hated Kan, beat him hundreds of times, and plotted to crush him with a sandbag; another jailer rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: A local boy in the jail hated him, lashed him hundreds of times, and tried to smother him with a sandbag until a fellow guard intervened.

sentences.zh: 柟居獄中，益讀所攜書，作《幽鞫》、《放招》二賦，詞旨沈郁。

translations.literal: In prison Kan read still more from the books he had brought and wrote the two rhapsodies "Dark Inquiry" and "Released Summons," grave and somber in diction.
translations.idiomatic: In his cell he read on and composed "Dark Inquiry" and "Released Summons," works of deep, mournful power.

sentences.zh: 謝榛入京師，見諸貴人，泣訴其冤狀曰：「生有一盧柟不能救，乃從千古哀沅而吊湘乎！

translations.literal: Xie Zhen entered the capital, saw the great men, and wept as he pleaded his unjust case, saying, "If I cannot save one Lu Kan alive, am I to follow the ancients in mourning Yuan and lamenting Xiang from afar?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhen came to the capital, sought the mighty, and wept: "If I cannot save Lu Kan, shall I only mourn Yuan and Xiang across the ages?"

sentences.zh: 」平湖陸光祖遷得浚令，因榛言平反其獄。

translations.literal: Lu Guangzu of Pinghu had just become magistrate of Jun and, on Zhen's word, reversed the case.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangzu of Pinghu, newly appointed magistrate of Jun, cleared the verdict on Zhen's appeal.

sentences.zh: 柟出，走謁榛。

translations.literal: Kan came out and ran to pay his respects to Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Released, Kan rushed to thank Zhen.

sentences.zh: 榛方客趙康王所，王立召見柟，禮為上賓。

translations.literal: Zhen was then a guest at Prince Kang's residence; the prince immediately summoned Kan and honored him as a chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was staying with Prince Kang, who at once received Kan and treated him as a principal guest.

sentences.zh: 諸宗人以王故爭客柟，柟酒酣罵座如故。

translations.literal: The clan relatives all vied to host Kan because of the prince; when drunk Kan reviled the company as before.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen fought to entertain him for the prince's sake; drunk, he abused the table as ever.

sentences.zh: 及光祖為南京禮部郎，柟往訪之，遍游吳會無所遇，還益落魄嗜酒，病三日卒。

translations.literal: When Guangzu became a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, Kan went to visit him, traveled widely through Wu and Kuaiji without meeting fortune, returned home ever more downcast and addicted to wine, and after three days' illness died.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangzu took a post in Nanjing Rites, Kan sought him out, wandered through the lower Yangtze without success, came home more broken and drunken than ever, and died after three days' sickness.

sentences.zh: 柟騷賦最為王世貞所稱，詩亦豪放如其為人。

translations.literal: Kan's sao and fu won the highest praise from Wang Shizhen; his poetry too was bold, like the man himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen prized Kan's sao and fu above all; his verse was as fierce as his character.

sentences.zh: 李攀龍附 梁有譽 等

translations.literal: Li Panlong appended: Liang Youyu and others
translations.idiomatic: Li Panlong; appended: Liang Youyu and others

sentences.zh: 李攀龍，字於鱗，歷城人。

translations.literal: Li Panlong, style name Yuqin, was a native of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Panlong, courtesy name Yuqin, came from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 九歲而孤，家貧，自奮於學。

translations.literal: Orphaned at nine, poor in family, he drove himself in study.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was nine; though poor, he drove himself through his books.

sentences.zh: 稍長為諸生，與友人許邦才、殷士儋學為詩歌。

translations.literal: Growing older he became a student, and with his friends Xu Bangcai and Yin Shidan studied to write poetry.
translations.idiomatic: As a student he joined Xu Bangcai and Yin Shidan in learning poetry.

sentences.zh: 已，益厭訓詁學，日讀古書，裡人共目為狂生。

translations.literal: Later he grew weary of exegetical learning, read ancient books daily, and his townsfolk all regarded him as a madman.
translations.idiomatic: He soon tired of philology, devoured the ancients each day, and neighbors called him mad.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉靖二十三年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Jiajing and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1544 and entered the Ministry of Justice as a director.

sentences.zh: 歷員外郎、郎中，稍遷順德知府，有善政。

translations.literal: He served as outside director and director, was gradually promoted to prefect of Shunde, and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ministry ranks, he became prefect of Shunde and governed with real kindness.

sentences.zh: 上官交薦，擢陝西提學副使。

translations.literal: His superiors jointly recommended him, and he was elevated to vice education intendant in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by his superiors, he was made Shaanxi vice education intendant.

sentences.zh: 鄉人殷學為巡撫，檄令屬文，攀龍怫然曰：「文可檄致邪？

translations.literal: His townsman Yin Xue was grand coordinator and ordered him by dispatch to compose a piece; Panlong said angrily, "Can literature be summoned by dispatch?"
translations.idiomatic: When his fellow townsman Yin Xue, now grand coordinator, demanded an essay by official letter, Panlong snapped, "Is literature to be ordered up like a clerk?"

sentences.zh: 」拒不應。

translations.literal: He refused and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: He refused outright.

sentences.zh: 會其地數震，攀龍心悸，念母思歸，遂謝病。

translations.literal: About that time the region suffered repeated earthquakes; Panlong's heart trembled, he thought of his mother and wished to return, and he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquakes shook the region; his nerves failed, he longed for his mother, and he asked leave on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 故事，外官謝病不再起，吏部重其才，用何景明便，特予告歸。

translations.literal: By precedent, an outer official who resigned on illness was not reappointed; the Ministry of Personnel valued his talent and, following the precedent for He Jingming, specially granted him leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Custom held that an outside officer who quit for illness never returned; the ministry, cherishing his gifts, followed He Jingming's case and allowed him home on special leave.

sentences.zh: 予告者，例得再起。

translations.literal: Those granted leave were by rule eligible to serve again.
translations.idiomatic: Such leave normally carried the right of recall.

sentences.zh: 攀龍既歸，構白雪樓，名日益高。

translations.literal: Once home, Panlong built the White Snow Tower, and his fame grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he raised the White Snow Tower, and his renown mounted day by day.

sentences.zh: 賓客造門，率謝不見，大吏至，亦然，以是得簡傲聲。

translations.literal: Guests who came to his door were generally refused audience; great officials were treated the same, and for this he gained a reputation for arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors were usually turned away—even grandees—and he won a name for haughtiness.

sentences.zh: 獨故交殷、許輩過從靡間。

translations.literal: Only old friends such as Yin and Xu came and went without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Only old companions like Yin and Xu still passed freely through his gate.

sentences.zh: 時徐中行亦家居，坐客恆滿，二人聞之，交相得也。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Zhongxing too was living at home with guests always filling his seats; when the two heard of each other they took a mutual liking.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhongxing also lived in retirement with a house always full; hearing of each other, the two men became fast friends.

sentences.zh: 歸田將十年，隆慶改元，薦起浙江副使，改參政，擢河南按察使。

translations.literal: After nearly ten years in retirement, when Longqing began its reign he was recommended and recalled as vice commissioner in Zhejiang, then made administration commissioner, and elevated to surveillance commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Near ten years at home, he was recalled at the Longqing accession as Zhejiang vice commissioner, then administration commissioner, then Henan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 攀龍至是摧亢為和，賓客亦稍稍進。

translations.literal: Panlong by then curbed his pride and grew affable, and guests gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had softened his bearing, and visitors slowly came back.

translations.literal: The source text here is damaged or lost.
translations.idiomatic: The narrative continues below after a lacuna in the original.

sentences.zh: 無何，奔母喪歸，哀毀得疾，疾少間，一日心痛卒。

translations.literal: Before long he rushed home on his mother's death; grief and fasting brought illness, and when the illness briefly eased he died one day of heart pain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his mother died; mourning broke his health, and when he seemed to mend, sudden heart pain killed him in a day.

sentences.zh: 攀龍之始官刑曹也，與濮州李先芳、臨清謝榛、孝豐吳維岳輩倡詩社。

translations.literal: When Panlong first served in the penal bureau he founded a poetry society with Li Xianfang of Puzhou, Xie Zhen of Linqing, and Wu Weiyue of Xiaofeng.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong's first post in Justice brought him together with Li Xianfang, Xie Zhen, and Wu Weiyue in a poetry club.

sentences.zh: 王世貞初釋褐，先芳引入社，遂與攀龍定交。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen had just left the examination hall; Xianfang brought him into the society, and he and Panlong formed a close bond.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen had just entered office; Xianfang introduced him to the club, and he and Panlong became intimate friends.

sentences.zh: 明年，先芳出為外吏。

translations.literal: The next year Xianfang went out as an outside official.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xianfang left for a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 又二年，宗臣、梁有譽入，是為五子。

translations.literal: Two years later Zongchen and Liang Youyu entered; these were the Five Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on, Zongchen and Liang Youyu joined—the Five Masters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徐中行、吳國倫亦至，乃改稱七子。

translations.literal: Before long Xu Zhongxing and Wu Guolun also arrived, and the name was changed to the Seven Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu Zhongxing and Wu Guolun came as well, and the group became the Seven Masters.

sentences.zh: 諸人多少年，才高氣銳，互相標榜，視當世無人，七才子之名播天下。

translations.literal: They were all young, of high talent and sharp spirit, praising one another and seeing no one in the age as their equal; the name Seven Talents spread through the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Young, brilliant, and fierce, they hailed one another and disdained their contemporaries until the Seven Talents were known everywhere.

sentences.zh: 擯先芳、維岳不與，已而榛亦被擯，攀龍遂為之魁。

translations.literal: They excluded Xianfang and Weiyue; later Zhen too was cast out, and Panlong became their chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfang and Weiyue were pushed aside; Zhen followed; Panlong stood at their head.

sentences.zh: 其持論謂文自西京，詩自天寶而下，俱無足觀，於本朝獨推李夢陽。

translations.literal: Their doctrine held that from the Western Han in prose and from the Tianbao era in poetry nothing was worth viewing; in their own dynasty they upheld Li Mengyang alone.
translations.idiomatic: They taught that prose after the Western Han and poetry after the Tianbao reign were worthless, and in the Ming they upheld Li Mengyang alone.

sentences.zh: 諸子翕然和之，非是，則詆為宋學。

translations.literal: The others chimed in together; whoever disagreed was reviled as a Song-dynasty pedant.
translations.idiomatic: The rest echoed him; dissent was mocked as Song learning.

sentences.zh: 攀龍才思勁鷙，名最高，獨心重世貞，天下亦並稱王、李。

translations.literal: Panlong's talent was fierce and his name highest; he alone held Shizhen in special regard, and the world paired Wang and Li together.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong's genius was savage and his fame supreme; he prized Shizhen above all, and the age spoke of Wang and Li in one breath.

sentences.zh: 又與李夢陽、何景明並稱何、李、王、李。

translations.literal: He was also grouped with Li Mengyang and He Jingming as He, Li, Wang, and Li.
translations.idiomatic: With Mengyang and He Jingming he formed the quartet He, Li, Wang, and Li.

sentences.zh: 其為詩，務以聲調勝，所擬樂府，或更古數字為己作，文則聱牙戟口，讀者至不能終篇。

translations.literal: In poetry he strove to win by tone; in the yuefu he imitated he sometimes altered a few ancient words and passed them off as his own; in prose his language was jagged and halting, and readers could not finish a piece.
translations.idiomatic: His verse aimed at sound; in ballads he sometimes rewrote a few archaic words as his own; his prose bit and stuck in the throat until readers could not finish a line.

sentences.zh: 好之者推為一代宗匠，亦多受世抉摘雲。

translations.literal: Admirers hailed him as the age's patriarch, yet many in the world picked him apart as well, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Followers called him master of the age; critics found much to fault, it is said.

sentences.zh: 自號滄溟。

translations.literal: He styled himself Cangming.
translations.idiomatic: He took the sobriquet Cangming.

sentences.zh: 梁有譽、宗臣、徐中行、吳國倫，皆嘉靖二十九年進士。

translations.literal: Liang Youyu, Zongchen, Xu Zhongxing, and Wu Guolun all passed the jinshi in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Youyu, Zongchen, Xu Zhongxing, and Wu Guolun all became jinshi in 1550.

sentences.zh: 有譽除刑部主事，居三年，以念母告歸，杜門讀書。

translations.literal: Youyu was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice; after three years he memorialized to return home on account of his mother and shut his door to read.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu served three years in Justice, then left to mourn his mother and read behind closed doors.

sentences.zh: 大吏至，辭不見。

translations.literal: When great officials came he declined to see them.
translations.idiomatic: He would not receive visiting grandees.

sentences.zh: 卒年三十六。

translations.literal: He died at thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 宗臣，字子相，揚州興化人。

translations.literal: Zongchen, style name Zixiang, was a native of Xinghua in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongchen, courtesy name Zixiang, came from Xinghua in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 由刑部主事調考功，謝病歸，築室百花洲上，讀書其中。

translations.literal: Transferred from a Justice director to the Merit Office, he resigned on illness, built a studio on Baihua Islet, and read within it.
translations.idiomatic: Moved from Justice to Merit, he quit for illness, built a study on Baihua Islet, and lived among his books.

sentences.zh: 起故官，移文選。

translations.literal: Recalled to his former post, he was moved to the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Called back, he was shifted to Appointments.

sentences.zh: 進稽勛員外郎，嚴嵩惡之，出為福建參議。

translations.literal: Promoted to outside director in the Merit Office, he was hated by Yan Song and sent out as administration commissioner in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the Merit Office, he earned Yan Song's enmity and was posted to Fujian as administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 倭薄城，臣守西門，納鄉人避難者萬人。

translations.literal: When pirates pressed the city, Zongchen guarded the west gate and admitted ten thousand townsfolk seeking refuge.
translations.idiomatic: As raiders neared the walls he held the west gate and sheltered ten thousand refugees.

sentences.zh: 或言賊且迫，曰：「我在，不憂賊也。

translations.literal: Some said the bandits were about to break in; he said, "While I am here, do not fear the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: When others warned the enemy was upon them, he said, "While I stand here, the pirates will not enter."

sentences.zh: 」與主者共擊退之。

translations.literal: Together with the commander he beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: He and the commander drove them off.

sentences.zh: 尋遷提學副使，卒官，士民皆哭。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice education intendant and died in office; officials and commoners all wept.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice education intendant, died in post, and gentry and people wept together.

sentences.zh: 徐中行，字子輿，長興人。

translations.literal: Xu Zhongxing, style name Ziyu, was a native of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhongxing, courtesy name Ziyu, came from Changxing.

sentences.zh: 美姿容，善飲酒。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing, he was skilled at drinking.
translations.idiomatic: He was fine-looking and a great drinker.

sentences.zh: 由刑部主事歷員外郎、郎中，稍遷汀州知府。

translations.literal: From a Justice director he served as outside director and director and was gradually promoted to prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Starting in Justice, he rose to outside director and director and became prefect of Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣東賊蕭五來犯，御之，有功。

translations.literal: The Guangdong bandit Xiao Wu came to attack; he resisted them with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangdong rebel Xiao Wu attacked, he repelled them with credit.

sentences.zh: 策其且走，俾武平令徐甫宰邀擊之，讓功甫宰，甫宰得優擢。

translations.literal: Judging that they would soon flee, he had the magistrate of Wuping, Xu Fu, lie in wait to intercept them and yielded the merit to Fu, who was specially promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing they would run, he set Magistrate Xu Fu of Wuping to ambush them and gave Fu the glory; Fu won a fine promotion.

sentences.zh: 尋以父憂歸，補汝寧，坐大計，貶長蘆鹽運判官。

translations.literal: Soon he returned on his father's mourning, was reassigned to Runan, and at the grand evaluation was demoted to salt transport judge at Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he served at Runan, then was demoted at review to salt transport judge at Changlu.

sentences.zh: 行湖廣僉事，掩捕湖盜柯彩鳳，得其積貯，活饑民萬余。

translations.literal: Serving as assistant surveillance commissioner in Huguang, he surprised and captured the lake pirate Ke Caifeng, seized his hoards, and kept more than ten thousand starving people alive.
translations.idiomatic: As Huguang assistant surveillance commissioner he seized the lake pirate Ke Caifeng, took his stores, and fed more than ten thousand hungry people.

sentences.zh: 累官江西左布政使，萬曆六年卒官。

translations.literal: He rose in successive offices to left administration commissioner of Jiangxi and died in office in the sixth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as left administration commissioner of Jiangxi and died in office in 1578.

sentences.zh: 中行性好客，無賢愚貴賤，應之不倦，故其死也，人多哀之。

translations.literal: Zhongxing loved to entertain guests and, whether worthy or foolish, noble or base, answered them tirelessly; therefore when he died many mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing welcomed all comers without weariness, noble or mean, wise or dull, and many grieved when he died.

sentences.zh: 吳國倫，字明卿，興國人。

translations.literal: Wu Guolun, style name Mingqing, was a native of Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guolun, courtesy name Mingqing, came from Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 由中書舍人擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: From a Secretariat draftsman he was promoted to a supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from the Secretariat, he became a war bureau supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 楊繼盛死，倡眾賻送，忤嚴嵩，假他事謫江西按察司知事。

translations.literal: When Yang Jisheng died he led the crowd in funeral gifts, offended Yan Song, and on a pretext was demoted to registrar of the Jiangxi surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jisheng's death he organized public mourning gifts, angered Yan Song, and was banished to a Jiangxi surveillance registrar's post on a trumped-up charge.

sentences.zh: 量移南康推官，調歸德，居二歲棄去。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate of Nankang, then to Guide, he left after two years.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Nankang magistrate and then Guide, he abandoned office after two years.

sentences.zh: 嵩敗，起建寧同知，累遷河南左參政，大計罷歸。

translations.literal: When Song fell he was recalled as assistant prefect of Jianning, rose to left administration commissioner of Henan, and was dismissed at the grand evaluation and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After Song's fall he returned as Jianning assistant prefect, rose to left Henan administration commissioner, and went home dismissed at review.

sentences.zh: 國倫才氣橫放，好客輕財。

translations.literal: Guolun's talent was bold and expansive; he loved guests and treated wealth lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Guolun was brimming with talent, hospitable, and careless of money.

sentences.zh: 歸田後聲名籍甚，求名之士，不東走太倉，則西走興國。

translations.literal: After returning home his fame was very great; seekers of reputation went east to Taicang or west to Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement his name thundered; ambitious youths went east to Taicang or west to Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，世貞既沒，國倫猶無恙，在七子中最為老壽。

translations.literal: In the Wanli era, after Shizhen had died, Guolun still remained; among the Seven Masters he lived longest.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli times, after Shizhen was gone, Guolun alone survived—the longest-lived of the Seven.

sentences.zh: 王世貞附 汪道昆 胡應麟 弟 世懋

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen appended: Wang Daokun, Hu Yinglin, and his brother Shimao
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen; appended: Wang Daokun, Hu Yinglin, and his brother Shimao

sentences.zh: 王世貞，字元美，太倉人，右都御史忬子也。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen, style name Yuanmei, was a native of Taicang and son of the Right Censor-in-Chief Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen, courtesy name Yuanmei, came from Taicang, son of Right Censor-in-Chief Wang Shi.

sentences.zh: 生有異稟，書過目，終身不忘。

translations.literal: Born with a singular gift, whatever book he passed before his eyes he never forgot for life.
translations.idiomatic: He was born with a prodigious memory: a book once seen was never forgotten.

sentences.zh: 年十九，舉嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: At nineteen he passed the jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he took the jinshi in 1547.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Justice as a director.

sentences.zh: 世貞好為詩古文，官京師，入王宗沐、李先芳、吳維岳等詩社，又與李攀龍、宗臣、梁有譽、徐中行、吳國倫輩相倡和，紹述何、李，名日益盛。

translations.literal: Shizhen loved to write ancient-style poetry and prose; in the capital he joined Wang Zongmu, Li Xianfang, and Wu Weiyue's poetry society, and with Li Panlong, Zongchen, Liang Youyu, Xu Zhongxing, and Wu Guolun he exchanged work, continuing the He and Li tradition, and his fame grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he joined the poetry clubs of Wang Zongmu, Li Xianfang, and Wu Weiyue, allied with Panlong and the Seven Masters, carried on He and Li, and grew ever more famous.

sentences.zh: 屢遷員外郎、郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to outside director and director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to outside director and director.

sentences.zh: 奸人閻姓者犯法，匿錦衣都督陸炳家，世貞搜得之。

translations.literal: A villain surnamed Yan broke the law and hid in the home of the embroidered-uniform guard Lu Bing; Shizhen searched him out and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: A criminal named Yan took refuge with Guard Commander Lu Bing; Shizhen found and arrested him.

sentences.zh: 炳介嚴嵩以請，不許。

translations.literal: Bing asked through Yan Song, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Bing pleaded through Yan Song, but Shizhen would not yield.

sentences.zh: 楊繼盛下吏，時進湯藥。

translations.literal: When Yang Jisheng was imprisoned he regularly sent him broth and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Jisheng lay in prison, Shizhen sent him food and medicine.

sentences.zh: 其妻訟夫冤，為代草。

translations.literal: When Yang's wife pleaded her husband's innocence, he drafted the petition for her.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the memorial for Yang's wife when she sued for her husband's innocence.

sentences.zh: 既死，復棺殮之。

translations.literal: After Yang died he coffined and buried him again.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang's execution he saw to a proper coffining and burial.

sentences.zh: 嵩大恨。

translations.literal: Song hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Song hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 吏部兩擬提學皆不用，用為青州兵備副使。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel twice nominated him for education intendant but he was not used; he was appointed vice commissioner for military affairs at Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Twice the ministry proposed him for education intendant and was refused; he was sent to Qingzhou as vice commissioner for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 父忬以濼河失事，嵩構之，論死系獄。

translations.literal: His father Shi was implicated in the Luo River disaster through Song's machinations, was sentenced to death, and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Shi was framed by Song over the Luo River affair, condemned to death, and jailed.

sentences.zh: 世貞解官奔赴，與弟世懋日蒲伏嵩門，涕泣求貸。

translations.literal: Shizhen resigned and rushed to him; he and his brother Shimao daily prostrated themselves at Song's gate, weeping and begging mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen quit office and ran to the capital; he and Shimao knelt daily at Song's gate in tears, begging for their father's life.

sentences.zh: 嵩陰持忬獄，而時為謾語以寬之。

translations.literal: Song secretly kept Shi's case pending while now and then speaking soothing words to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Song kept the case hanging while murmuring words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 兩人又日囚服跽道旁，遮諸貴人輿，搏顙乞救。

translations.literal: The two brothers again daily wore convict garb and knelt by the road, stopping the carriages of the great and beating their foreheads to beg rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Daily they wore prison dress and knelt by the road, halting nobles' carriages and kowtowing for help.

sentences.zh: 諸貴人畏嵩不敢言，忬竟死西市。

translations.literal: The nobles feared Song and dared not speak; Shi was executed at last in the western market.
translations.idiomatic: The great men feared Song and were silent; Shi died at the western market.

sentences.zh: 兄弟哀號欲絕，持喪歸，蔬食三年，不入內寢。

translations.literal: The brothers wailed as if their breath would break; they carried the coffin home, ate vegetables for three years, and did not enter the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers' grief nearly killed them; they bore the body home, ate plain food for three years, and never entered the women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 既除服，猶卻冠帶，苴履葛巾，不赴宴會。

translations.literal: When mourning ended they still refused cap and belt, wore hemp shoes and a cloth turban, and did not attend banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Even after mourning they shunned official dress, wore hemp sandals and plain cloth, and avoided feasts.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年八月，兄弟伏闕訟父冤，言為嵩所害，大學士徐階左右之，復忬官。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Longqing the brothers knelt at the palace gate to sue for their father's wrong, saying he had been murdered by Song; Grand Secretary Xu Jie supported them, and Shi's office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing's first year they knelt at the gate to accuse Song of murdering their father; Xu Jie aided them, and Shi's honor was restored.

sentences.zh: 世貞意不欲出，會詔求直言，疏陳法祖宗、正殿名、慶恩義、寬禁例、修典章、推德意、昭爵賞、練兵實八事，以應詔。

translations.literal: Shizhen was unwilling to take office, but when an edict sought forthright counsel he memorialized on eight matters—honoring the ancestral laws, correcting palace names, celebrating grace, easing prohibitions, repairing statutes, extending virtue, clarifying enfeoffments and rewards, and strengthening military reality—in answer to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Reluctant to serve, he answered the call for frank counsel with eight reforms touching law, ritual, grace, prohibitions, statutes, virtue, honors, and military strength.

sentences.zh: 無何，吏部用言官薦，令以副使涖大名。

translations.literal: Before long the Ministry of Personnel, on censors' recommendation, ordered him to take up Daming as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the ministry, on censors' advice, sent him to Daming as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江右參政，山西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right administration commissioner in Zhejiang and surveillance commissioner in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became right administration commissioner in Zhejiang and surveillance commissioner in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服除，補湖廣，旋改廣西右布政使，入為太僕卿。

translations.literal: He returned on his mother's mourning; when mourning ended he was reassigned to Huguang, soon changed to right administration commissioner in Guangxi, and entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he served in Huguang, moved to right Guangxi administration commissioner, and entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年九月以右副都御史撫治鄖陽，數條奏屯田、戍守、兵食事宜，咸切大計。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Wanli he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to pacify and govern Yunyang, repeatedly memorializing on garrison farming, frontier defense, and army provisions—all hitting the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 2 he became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief for Yunyang and sent memorial after memorial on farming garrisons, defense, and rations, each striking the heart of policy.

sentences.zh: 有奸僧偽稱樂平王次子，奉高皇帝御容、金牒，行游天下。

translations.literal: A wicked monk falsely claimed to be the second son of the Prince of Leping, carrying the Gaozu emperor's portrait and a gold patent, and traveled through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A false monk posed as the Prince of Leping's second son, bearing the Hongwu emperor's image and a golden warrant, and wandered the empire.

sentences.zh: 世貞曰：「宗籓不得出城，而訁壽張如此，必偽也。

translations.literal: Shizhen said, "Clan princes may not leave the city walls; to sue for longevity at Shouzhang in this fashion must be a fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen said, "Imperial clansmen may not leave their cities; to seek long life at Shouzhang in this way must be imposture."

sentences.zh: 」捕訊之，服辜。

translations.literal: He arrested and examined the man, who confessed his crime.
translations.idiomatic: He seized and interrogated the man, who confessed.

sentences.zh: 張居正枋國，以世貞同年生，有意引之，世貞不甚親附。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng held the state; as Shizhen was a fellow graduate of the same year, Juzheng wished to draw him near, but Shizhen was not very intimate or attached.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng ruled the realm; though they had taken the jinshi together, Shizhen kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 所部荊州地震，引京房占，謂臣道太盛，坤維不寧，用以諷居正。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction Jingzhou suffered an earthquake; citing Jing Fang's divination he said ministerial power was too great and the earth's southwest was unsettled, using this to admonish Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou shook, he cited Jing Fang to say that excessive ministerial power disturbed the southwest of the earth—a pointed warning to Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 居正婦弟辱江陵令，世貞論奏不少貸。

translations.literal: Juzheng's wife's younger brother insulted the magistrate of Jiangling; Shizhen memorialized against him without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng's brother-in-law abused the magistrate of Jiangling, Shizhen impeached him without mercy.

sentences.zh: 居正積不能堪，會遷南京大理卿，為給事中楊節所劾，即取旨罷之。

translations.literal: Juzheng could not bear it cumulatively; when Shizhen was transferred to Nanjing as president of the Grand Court, Supervising Secretary Yang Jie impeached him, and an edict at once dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's resentment mounted; when Shizhen moved to Nanjing as Grand Court president, Yang Jie impeached him and the throne dismissed him at once.

sentences.zh: 後起應天府尹，復被劾罷。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled as prefect of Yingtian and was again impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Yingtian prefect, he was impeached and removed again.

sentences.zh: 居正歿，起南京刑部右侍郎，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died he was raised to Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing but declined on illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng died he was offered Nanjing Vice Minister of Justice but pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 久之，所善王錫爵秉政，起南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long while his friend Wang Xizhe held power and recalled him as Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Years later his ally Wang Xizhe governed and called him back as Nanjing Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 先是，世貞為副都御史及大理卿、應天尹與侍郎，品皆正三。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shizhen had been vice censor-in-chief, Grand Court president, Yingtian prefect, and vice minister, his rank had all been regular third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, as vice censor-in-chief, Grand Court president, Yingtian prefect, and vice minister, he had held regular third rank.

sentences.zh: 世貞通理前俸，得考滿陰子。

translations.literal: Shizhen reckoned his prior salaries together and qualified for the privilege of yin enfeoffment for a son at the full evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He counted his earlier salaries and at review qualified to enfeoff a son by yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 比擢南京刑部尚書，御史黃仁榮言世貞先被劾，不當計俸，據故事力爭。

translations.literal: When he was promoted to Minister of Justice at Nanjing, Censor Huang Renrong said that since Shizhen had earlier been impeached he should not count salary; he strove according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Nanjing Minister of Justice, Censor Huang Renrong argued that prior impeachment barred counting service; he fought by precedent.

sentences.zh: 世貞乃三疏移疾歸。

translations.literal: Shizhen then submitted three memorials citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen sent three memorials pleading illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 二十一年卒於家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in 1593.

sentences.zh: 世貞始與李攀龍狎主文盟，攀龍歿，獨操柄二十年。

translations.literal: Shizhen at first shared leadership of the literary alliance with Li Panlong; after Panlong died he alone held the scepter for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He first shared literary rule with Panlong; after Panlong's death he alone led the field for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 才最高，地望最顯，聲華意氣籠蓋海內。

translations.literal: His talent was highest, his position most eminent, and his brilliance and spirit covered the empire.
translations.idiomatic: His gifts, rank, and aura overshadowed the realm.

sentences.zh: 一時士大夫及山人、詞客、衲子、羽流，莫不奔走門下。

translations.literal: For a time grandees, mountain men, lyric guests, monks, and Daoist priests all hurried to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars, recluses, poets, monks, and Daoists all flocked to his door.

sentences.zh: 片言褒賞，聲價驟起。

translations.literal: A word of praise from him and one's price rose at once.
translations.idiomatic: A single word of praise from him could make a reputation overnight.

sentences.zh: 其持論，文必西漢，詩必盛唐，大歷以後書勿讀，而藻飾太甚。

translations.literal: His doctrine held that prose must be Western Han and poetry must be High Tang; books after the Dali reign were not to be read, yet his ornamentation was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: He held that prose must be Western Han and poetry High Tang, scorned post-Dali work, yet gilded his own writing too heavily.

sentences.zh: 晚年，攻者漸起，世貞顧漸造平淡。

translations.literal: In his later years attackers gradually arose, and Shizhen turned toward plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life critics multiplied, and he moved toward a plainer style.

sentences.zh: 病亟時，劉鳳往視，見其手蘇子瞻集，諷玩不置也。

translations.literal: When gravely ill, Liu Feng came to visit and saw him holding Su Dongpo's collected works, reading them with delight and unable to set them down.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Liu Feng found him clutching Su Dongpo's collected works, unable to stop reading.

sentences.zh: 世貞自號鳳洲，又號弇州山人。

translations.literal: Shizhen styled himself Lord of Phoenix Islet and also Mountain Man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He called himself Lord of Phoenix Islet and the Mountain Man of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 其所與游者，大抵見其集中，各為標目。

translations.literal: Those with whom he associated are largely seen in his collected works, each given a label.
translations.idiomatic: His companions are catalogued in his collected works under set titles.

sentences.zh: 曰前五子者，攀龍、中行、有譽、國倫、臣也。

translations.literal: The Former Five Masters were Panlong, Zhongxing, Youyu, Guolun, and Zongchen.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Five were Panlong, Zhongxing, Youyu, Guolun, and Zongchen.

sentences.zh: 後五子則南昌余曰德、蒲圻魏裳、歙汪道昆、銅梁張佳胤、新蔡張九一也。

translations.literal: The Latter Five Masters were Yu Yuede of Nanchang, Wei Shang of Puqi, Wang Daokun of She County, Zhang Jiayin of Tongliang, and Zhang Jiuyi of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: The Latter Five were Yu Yuede of Nanchang, Wei Shang of Puqi, Wang Daokun of She, Zhang Jiayin of Tongliang, and Zhang Jiuyi of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 廣五子則昆山俞允文、浚盧柟、濮州李先芳、孝豐吳維岳、順德歐大任也。

translations.literal: The Broad Five Masters were Yu Yunwen of Kunshan, Lu Kan of Jun, Li Xianfang of Puzhou, Wu Weiyue of Xiaofeng, and Ou Daren of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: The Broad Five were Yu Yunwen of Kunshan, Lu Kan of Jun, Li Xianfang of Puzhou, Wu Weiyue of Xiaofeng, and Ou Daren of Shunde.

sentences.zh: 續五子則陽曲王道行、東明石星、從化黎民表、南昌硃多火煃、常熟趙用賢也。

translations.literal: The Continued Five Masters were Wang Daoxing of Yangqu, Shi Xing of Dongming, Li Minbiao of Conghua, Zhu Duohuo of Nanchang, and Zhao Yongxian of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: The Continued Five were Wang Daoxing of Yangqu, Shi Xing of Dongming, Li Minbiao of Conghua, Zhu Duohuo of Nanchang, and Zhao Yongxian of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 末五子則京山李維楨、鄞屠隆、南樂魏允中、蘭溪胡應麟，而用賢復與焉。

translations.literal: The Final Five Masters were Li Weizhen of Jingshan, Tu Long of Yin, Wei Yunzhong of Nanle, Hu Yinglin of Lanxi—and Yongxian was counted again.
translations.idiomatic: The Final Five were Li Weizhen of Jingshan, Tu Long of Yin, Wei Yunzhong of Nanle, Hu Yinglin of Lanxi, with Yongxian listed twice.

sentences.zh: 其所去取，頗以好惡為高下。

translations.literal: Whom he kept or cast aside he often ranked high or low according to his likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: His lists rose and fell largely with his personal favor.

sentences.zh: 余曰德，字德甫，張佳胤，字肖甫，張九一，字助甫，世貞詩所謂「吾黨有三甫」也。

translations.literal: Yu Yuede, style name Defu; Zhang Jiayin, style name Xiaofu; Zhang Jiuyi, style name Zhufu—these were the "three fus" of his party in his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuede (Defu), Zhang Jiayin (Xiaofu), and Zhang Jiuyi (Zhufu) were the "three fus" of his circle.

sentences.zh: 魏裳，字順甫，與曰德俱嘉靖二十九年進士。

translations.literal: Wei Shang, style name Shunfu, and Yuede both passed the jinshi in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shang, courtesy name Shunfu, and Yuede both took the jinshi in 1550.

sentences.zh: 曰德終福建副使，裳終濟南知府。

translations.literal: Yuede ended as vice commissioner in Fujian; Shang ended as prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuede finished as Fujian vice commissioner; Shang as Jinan prefect.

sentences.zh: 九一，嘉靖三十二年進士，終巡撫寧夏僉都御史。

translations.literal: Jiuyi passed the jinshi in the thirty-second year of Jiajing and ended as Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyi became a jinshi in 1553 and died as censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 佳胤自有傳。

translations.literal: Jiayin has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiayin has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 汪道昆，字伯玉，世貞同年進士。

translations.literal: Wang Daokun, style name Boyu, was a fellow graduate of the same year as Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daokun, courtesy name Boyu, took the jinshi the same year as Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正亦其同年生也，父七十壽，道昆文當其意，居正亟稱之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng was also a fellow of the same year; for his father's seventieth birthday Daokun's essay pleased him, and Juzheng praised it repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng was their classmate; Daokun's piece for Juzheng's father's seventieth birthday delighted him and won repeated praise.

sentences.zh: 世貞筆之《藝苑卮》曰：「文繁而有法者於鱗，簡而有法者伯玉。

translations.literal: Shizhen wrote in "Art Garden Goblet": "For prose elaborate yet governed, Yuqin; simple yet governed, Boyu."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen wrote in the "Art Garden Goblet": "Elaborate but disciplined—Yuqin; plain but disciplined—Boyu."

sentences.zh: 」道昆由是名大起。

translations.literal: Daokun's name thereupon rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Daokun's fame soared.

sentences.zh: 晚年官兵部左侍郎，世貞亦嘗貳兵部，天下稱「兩司馬」。

translations.literal: In his later years he reached Left Vice Minister of War; Shizhen had also served as deputy in War, and the world called them the "Two Marshals."
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he became Left Vice Minister of War; Shizhen too had served in War, and people called them the "Two Marshals."

sentences.zh: 世貞頗不樂，嘗自悔獎道昆為違心之論雲。

translations.literal: Shizhen was quite displeased and once regretted that praising Daokun had been words against his heart, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen resented the pairing and reportedly regretted praising Daokun as flattery against his conscience.

sentences.zh: 胡應麟，幼能詩。

translations.literal: Hu Yinglin could compose poetry while still young.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yinglin wrote poetry from childhood.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年舉於鄉，久不第，築室山中，構書四萬余卷，手自編次，多所撰著。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wanli he passed the provincial examination but long failed the metropolitan; he built a studio in the mountains, assembled more than forty thousand volumes, arranged them with his own hand, and wrote many works.
translations.idiomatic: He won the provincial degree in 1576 but never passed the metropolitan; he built a mountain studio, gathered forty thousand books, catalogued them himself, and wrote abundantly.

sentences.zh: 攜詩謁世貞，世貞喜而激賞之，歸益自負。

translations.literal: He brought his poems to visit Shizhen; Shizhen rejoiced and praised them highly, and on returning Yinglin was still more self-assured.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting his verse to Shizhen, he was warmly praised and came home prouder than ever.

sentences.zh: 所著《詩藪》二十卷，大抵奉世貞《卮言》為律令，而敷衍其說，謂詩家之有世貞，集大成之尼父也。

translations.literal: His "Forest of Poetry" in twenty rolls largely took Shizhen's "Goblet Words" as law and elaborated the doctrine, saying that in poetry Shizhen was the Confucius who brought all traditions together.
translations.idiomatic: His twenty-juan "Forest of Poetry" treated Shizhen's "Goblet Words" as canon and declared him the Confucius who summed up all poetic schools.

sentences.zh: 其貢諛如此。

translations.literal: His flattery went so far.
translations.idiomatic: His adulation went that far.

sentences.zh: 世貞弟世懋，字敬美。

translations.literal: Shizhen's younger brother Shimao, style name Jingmei.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen's brother Shimao, courtesy name Jingmei.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年成進士，即遭父憂。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing he became a jinshi and at once met his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in 1559 and immediately entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 父雪，始選南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: When the wrong was cleared he was first chosen as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's name was cleared he entered the Nanjing Ministry of Rites as a director.

sentences.zh: 歷陝西、福建提學副使，再遷太常少卿，先世貞三年卒。

translations.literal: He served as vice education intendant in Shaanxi and Fujian, was twice promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and died three years before Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice education intendant in Shaanxi and Fujian, rose twice to Vice Minister of Sacrifices, and died three years before his brother.

sentences.zh: 好學，善詩文，名亞其兄。

translations.literal: Fond of learning, skilled in poetry and prose, his name was second only to his brother's.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and wrote well; his fame stood just below his brother's.

sentences.zh: 世貞力推引之，以為勝己，攀龍、道昆輩因稱為「少美」。

translations.literal: Shizhen strongly promoted him, thinking him superior to himself; Panlong, Daokun, and the others therefore called him "Young Mei."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen pushed him forward as better than himself; Panlong and Daokun called him "Young Mei."

sentences.zh: 世貞子士騏，字冏伯，舉鄉試第一，登萬曆十七年進士，終吏部員外郎，亦能文。

translations.literal: Shizhen's son Shiqi, style name Jiongbai, placed first in the provincial examination, passed the jinshi in the seventeenth year of Wanli, ended as an outside director in the Ministry of Personnel, and could also write well.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiqi, courtesy name Jiongbai, topped the provincial lists, became a jinshi in 1589, rose to an outside director in Personnel, and wrote ably.

sentences.zh: 歸有光子 子慕 附 胡友信

translations.literal: Gui Youguang's son Zimu appended: Hu Youxin
translations.idiomatic: Gui Youguang; his son Zimu; appended: Hu Youxin

sentences.zh: 歸有光，字熙甫，昆山人。

translations.literal: Gui Youguang, style name Xifu, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Youguang, courtesy name Xifu, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬文，弱冠盡通《五經》、《三史》諸書，師事同邑魏校。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose prose; in young manhood he mastered the Five Classics, the Three Histories, and other books, and studied under his townsman Wei Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he wrote prose; in youth he mastered the Five Classics, the Three Histories, and more, studying under Wei Jiao of his district.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十九年舉鄉試，八上春官不第。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiajing he passed the provincial examination and eight times went up to the metropolitan examination without placing.
translations.idiomatic: He won the provincial degree in 1540 and failed the metropolitan examination eight times.

sentences.zh: 徙居嘉定安亭江上，讀書談道。

translations.literal: He moved to live on the Anting River in Jiading, reading and discussing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Jiading on the Anting River to read and teach.

sentences.zh: 學徒常數百人，稱為震川先生。

translations.literal: His pupils often numbered in the hundreds; he was called Master Zhenchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of students gathered; they called him Master Zhenchuan.

sentences.zh: 四十四年始成進士，授長興知縣。

translations.literal: Only in the forty-fourth year did he finally become a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: He finally passed the jinshi in 1565 and was made magistrate of Changxing.

sentences.zh: 用古教化為治。

translations.literal: He governed with ancient rites and moral transformation.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled through ritual and moral example in the ancient manner.

sentences.zh: 每聽訟，引婦女兒童案前，刺刺作吳語，斷訖遣去，不具獄。

translations.literal: Whenever he heard cases he brought women and children before the bench, questioned them in rapid Wu speech, decided the matter, and sent them away without drawing up a written record.
translations.idiomatic: At trial he called women and children forward, questioned them in plain Wu dialect, ruled, and dismissed them without formal writs.

sentences.zh: 大吏令不便，輒寢閣不行。

translations.literal: When great officials gave orders he found inconvenient, he often shelved them unexecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Orders from superiors that struck him as wrong he often left unexecuted in his desk.

sentences.zh: 有所擊斷，直行己意。

translations.literal: When he did strike a decision he carried out his own intent straight through.
translations.idiomatic: When he did act, he acted on his own judgment.

sentences.zh: 大吏多惡之，調順德通判，專轄馬政。

translations.literal: Many great officials hated him; he was transferred to assistant prefect of Shunde with sole charge of horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors resented him; he was moved to Shunde as assistant prefect in charge of horse administration only.

sentences.zh: 明世，進士為令無遷卒者，名為遷，實重抑之也。

translations.literal: In the Ming, no jinshi serving as magistrate had ever been promoted or demoted to the end of his term; though called a transfer, it was in fact a heavy demotion.
translations.idiomatic: No Ming jinshi magistrate had ever been promoted or dismissed at term's end; though termed a transfer, it was real disgrace.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，大學士高拱、趙貞吉雅知有光，引為南京太僕丞，留掌內閣制敕房，修《世宗實錄》，卒官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing Grand Secretaries Gao Gong and Zhao Zhenji, who knew Youguang well, brought him in as Vice Director of the Nanjing Imperial Stud, kept him in the Secretariat to manage imperial rescripts, and had him compile the "Veritable Records of Shizong"; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1570 Gao Gong and Zhao Zhenji, who knew him, made him Nanjing Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, kept him in the Secretariat drafting edicts, and set him to the Shizong Veritable Records; he died in post.

sentences.zh: 有光為古文，原本經術，好《太史公書》，得其神理。

translations.literal: Youguang wrote ancient prose rooted in the classics, loved the "Records of the Grand Historian," and grasped its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His prose grew from the classics; he loved Sima Qian and caught his spirit.

sentences.zh: 時王世貞主盟文壇，有光力相觸排，目為妄庸巨子。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shizhen led the literary world; Youguang forcefully opposed him and called him a deluded, mediocre chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen then ruled the literary world; Youguang openly fought him and called him a vain, second-rate pontiff.

sentences.zh: 世貞大憾，其後亦心折有光，為之贊曰：「千載有公，繼韓、歐陽。

translations.literal: Shizhen was deeply resentful; later he too came to admire Youguang and praised him, saying, "For a thousand years there is this man, successor to Han and Ouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen was stung, yet later bowed to Youguang and wrote, "For a thousand years there has been such a man—heir to Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 余豈異趨，久而自傷。

translations.literal: Am I of another path? Long I have grieved alone."
translations.idiomatic: Was I not of his way? Long have I hurt for it alone."

sentences.zh: 」其推重如此。

translations.literal: His esteem went so far.
translations.idiomatic: He honored him to that degree.

sentences.zh: 有光少子子慕，字季思。

translations.literal: Youguang's younger son Zimu, style name Jisi.
translations.idiomatic: Youguang's son Zimu, courtesy name Jisi.

sentences.zh: 舉萬曆十九年鄉試，再被放，即屏居江村，與無錫高攀龍最善。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the nineteenth year of Wanli, was twice failed at the metropolitan examination, then lived in seclusion in the river village, and was closest to Gao Panlong of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: He won the provincial degree in 1591, failed the metropolitan exam twice, retired to the river village, and was closest to Gao Panlong of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 其歿也，巡按御史祁彪佳請於朝，贈翰林待詔。

translations.literal: After his death Surveillance Commissioner Qi Bujia petitioned the court, and he was posthumously granted Hanlin awaiting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Qi Bujia memorialized the throne and he was posthumously made Hanlin awaiting edicts.

sentences.zh: 有光制舉義，湛深經術，卓然成大家。

translations.literal: Youguang's examination essays were steeped in the classics and stood as a great master.
translations.idiomatic: Youguang's civil-examination prose was deeply classical and made him a master.

sentences.zh: 後德清胡友信與齊名，世並稱歸、胡。

translations.literal: Later Hu Youxin of Deqing was famed equally with him, and the age paired them as Gui and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hu Youxin of Deqing shared his fame; the age spoke of Gui and Hu together.

sentences.zh: 友信，字成之，隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: Youxin, style name Chengzhi, passed the jinshi in the second year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: Youxin, courtesy name Chengzhi, became a jinshi in 1568.

sentences.zh: 授順德知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Shunde.

sentences.zh: 歲賦率奸胥攬輸，稍以所入啖長吏，謂之月錢。

translations.literal: The annual levy was usually monopolized by corrupt clerks who delivered the tax and skimmed a little for the senior officials—called "monthly money."
translations.idiomatic: Yearly taxes were usually cornered by venal clerks who delivered the grain and slipped a portion to their superiors as "monthly money."

sentences.zh: 友信與民約，歲為三限，多寡皆自輸，不取贏，閭里無妄費，而公賦以充。

translations.literal: Youxin made a pact with the people: each year three deadlines, each household paying directly whatever was owed, taking no surplus; the neighborhood had no waste, and public levies were met.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed with the people on three annual installments, direct payment without padding; villages wasted nothing and the treasury was filled.

sentences.zh: 海寇竊發，官軍往討，民間驛騷。

translations.literal: Sea bandits stirred; when government troops went to punish them the countryside was thrown into alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal pirates rose; official campaigns threw the district into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 部內烏洲、大洲，賊所巢穴，諸惡少為賊耳目。

translations.literal: Within the district were Wuzhou and Dazhou, nests of the bandits, and many young ruffians served as their eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou and Dazhou in his county were pirate lairs, and local toughs spied for them.

sentences.zh: 友信悉勾得之，捕誅其魁，余黨解散。

translations.literal: Youxin tracked them all down, executed the ringleaders, and the rest dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Youxin traced every informer, executed the chiefs, and the gangs broke up.

sentences.zh: 鄉立四應社，一鄉有警，三鄉鼓而援之，不援者罪同賊，賊不敢發。

translations.literal: He established the Four Responses Society in each village: if one village had an alarm, three villages would drum and come to aid; those who did not aid were guilty as bandits, and the bandits dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: He organized Four Responses societies—one village's alarm brought three villages drumming to the rescue; refusal equaled treason, and pirates dared not strike.

sentences.zh: 歲大凶，民飢死無敢為惡者。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine people starved to death yet none dared do evil.
translations.idiomatic: In a terrible famine people died of hunger, yet none turned to crime.

sentences.zh: 初，友信慮民輕法，涖以嚴，後令行禁止，更為寬大，或旬日不笞一人。

translations.literal: At first Youxin feared the people held the law lightly and governed with severity; later, when orders ran and prohibitions stood, he turned lenient and sometimes went ten days without a single beating.
translations.idiomatic: At first he ruled sternly lest the people despise the law; when order held he softened, sometimes passing ten days without a flogging.

sentences.zh: 其治縣如家，弊修墮舉，學校城池，咸為更新。

translations.literal: He governed the county like a household: what was broken he repaired, what had fallen he raised; schools and walls were all renewed.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the county like a home—repairing what was ruined, renewing schools and walls alike.

sentences.zh: 督課邑子弟，教化興起。

translations.literal: He supervised the district's young men and roused them through education.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled the local youth and lifted them through teaching.

sentences.zh: 卒官，士民立祠奉祀。

translations.literal: He died in office; officials and commoners erected a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post; gentry and people built a shrine in his memory.

sentences.zh: 友信博通經史，學有根柢。

translations.literal: Youxin was broadly versed in the classics and histories and his learning had deep roots.
translations.idiomatic: Youxin knew classics and histories thoroughly and his scholarship ran deep.

sentences.zh: 明代舉子業最擅名者，前則王鏊、唐順之，後則震川、思泉。

translations.literal: Among Ming candidates for literary fame, the earlier masters were Wang Ao and Tang Shunzhi; the later were Zhenchuan and Siquan.
translations.idiomatic: Of Ming writers famed in the examination tradition, Wang Ao and Tang Shunzhi came first; Zhenchuan and Siquan followed.

sentences.zh: 思泉，友信別號也。

translations.literal: Siquan was Youxin's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Siquan was Youxin's style name.
